- open OBS

title: XWayland windows have wonky focus
body:
Mouse focus doesn't work correctly on overlapping XWayland windows.

Examples:
Any XWayland app that opens a "open file..." dialog (GTK/QT?) e.g. VScode. When opening, you'll have to drag the window outside its parent for it to gain mouse focus.

VLC. Fullscreen it and try to interact with anything that isnt the main display surface (e.g. the control panel on the bottom, right click menu)

Only mouse focus is broken. Keyboard focus works as intended.

Should search in [CInputManager::mouseMoveUnified](https://github.com/vaxerski/Hyprland/blob/main/src/managers/InputManager.cpp#L21-L113)

title: Wiki:Installation page - Arch Linux required packages are incorrect
body:
The page for installation has a command for installing all the required dependencies on Arch, and the command includes `xcb-xfixes x11-xcb xcb-composite xcb-xinput xcb-render` which aren't actual packages.
The correct package names are `libxfixes libx11 libxcomposite xorg-xinput libxrender`

So the correct command would be `yay -S gdb ninja gcc cmake libxcb xcb-proto xcb-util xcb-util-keysyms libxfixes libx11 libxcomposite xorg-xinput libxrender pixman wayland-protocols wlroots-git`

Thanks

title: SUPERSHIFT bind doesn't work with Number KEY
body:
**Describe the bug**
Binding a number key (0-9) with the SUPERSHIFT modifier does not work. The keybind remains unresponsive. This key combination is a fairly common default for moving windows between workspaces in other WM's, so it's non-functionality may be confusing to some users. 

For example, the following config block does not work as intended:

```
bind=SUPERSHIFT,1,movetoworkspace,1
bind=SUPERSHIFT,2,movetoworkspace,2
bind=SUPERSHIFT,3,movetoworkspace,3
bind=SUPERSHIFT,4,movetoworkspace,4
bind=SUPERSHIFT,5,movetoworkspace,5
bind=SUPERSHIFT,6,movetoworkspace,6
bind=SUPERSHIFT,7,movetoworkspace,7
bind=SUPERSHIFT,8,movetoworkspace,8
bind=SUPERSHIFT,9,movetoworkspace,9
bind=SUPERSHIFT,0,movetoworkspace,10
```

The problem appears to be that the holding SHIFT+(0-9) returns the special character for that number key, rather than the actual number, and hyprland doesn't associate the special character keypress with the matching number key (sorry if I'm explaining this poorly, not sure of the proper terminology). An effective workaround is to specify the special character key, rather than the number key, in the config. For example, the following config block currently achieves the desired results for SUPERSHIFT+(0-9)

```
bind=SUPERSHIFT,exclam,movetoworkspace,1
bind=SUPERSHIFT,at,movetoworkspace,2
bind=SUPERSHIFT,numbersign,movetoworkspace,3
bind=SUPERSHIFT,dollar,movetoworkspace,4
bind=SUPERSHIFT,percent,movetoworkspace,5
bind=SUPERSHIFT,asciicircum,movetoworkspace,6
bind=SUPERSHIFT,ampersand,movetoworkspace,7
bind=SUPERSHIFT,asterisk,movetoworkspace,8
bind=SUPERSHIFT,parenleft,movetoworkspace,9
bind=SUPERSHIFT,parenright,movetoworkspace,10
```

Ideally I think these special character keys should be associated with their matched number keys so that the first config block would achieve the same results as the second. However, if this behavior is intended or otherwise non-trivial to correct, I think this should at least be documented in the wiki to alleviate some confusion.

title: Forgotten cd in Wiki/Installation
body: **Describe in detail your idea.** Hi! I was installing your awesome work and found out a small issue with the docs. https://github.com/vaxerski/Hyprland/wiki/Installation Issue is very simple, there's no cd after git clone so people will get the following error: ``make: *** No rule to make target 'install'. Stop.`` So it should be: ``` git clone https://github.com/vaxerski/Hyprland cd Hyprland sudo make install ```

title: Tabbed containers
body:
**Describe in detail your idea.**
My primary usecase of i3/sway is being able to ~~stack~~ tab windows in a container. I have a super ultra wide monitor and I have 3 columns of windows with my 'main' window in the middle. I always make this a ~~stacked~~ tabbed container so I can easily switch from my web browser / terminal / steam / game all being in the middle of my monitor. It's also nice just to declutter spare windows.

It has similar usecases as workspaces, but since my monitor is so wide I don't need an entire new screen of windows, I just want to easily repurpose my main area.

This is important to me and I'm unlikely to switch to this as my main wm unless this is a feature. Other than that though, it really is quite a nice experience! About time we had a fresh wm!

title: Some Applications fail to Autostart
body:
**Describe the bug**
Some applications fail to Autostart, or start in an unusable state when launched using `exec=` or `exec_once=`. This includes:

- `swaybg` fails to load on first launch after reboot. Reloading the config or logging out and back in resolves
- `foot --server` loads and runs in background, but is inaccessible to `footclient`. Client reports no server running
- Electron applications (Discord, Element, Caprine) fail to load entirely.

There are times where it is necessary to turn off a display. For example, on a VR headset, you do not want it acting as part of the desktop, so it is best to turn it off. It also seems to break certain parts of my main monitor's tiling while I have my HMD plugged in.

title: damange_tracking warning (config file parsing error)
body:
Upon starting Hyprland a blue warning appears at the top of the screen

```
Invalid value for general:damage_tracking, supported: full, monitor, none
Hyprland may not work correctly.
```

When looking at the configuration file damage_tracking is set to `none`

```
general {
    max_fps=60
    sensitivity=0.25
    main_mod=SUPER

    gaps_in=5
    gaps_out=20
    border_size=2
    col.active_border=0x66ee1111
    col.inactive_border=0x66333333

    damage_tracking=none # experimental, might have bugs!
}
```

However removing the comment `# experimental, might have bugs!` seems to fix the issue.
I'm assuming that the parsed value for the field includes the whole comment rather than just `none`.

Workspace's Group
body:
Good day to you!

i would like to describe my suggestion for implementation of groupping workspaces (maybe i've peeked it in i3/sway thread)

i think it's the best way to not overload `Hyprland` with specific functions and also include some useful in many ways tools:

1. Named workspaces (tags):
```
 so we can store multiple workspaces > [0..9]
 ```
2. ability to map keybindings by `hyprctl`:  
```
by default we map keys for `default` group of workspaces and by executing script for switching to another group, we remap this keybindings for another set of workspaces and unbind some, if there is such
```
like, 
```conf
# by default
bind=SUPER,1,workspace,default.1
bind=SUPER,2,workspace,default.2
bind=SUPER,3,workspace,default.3
...
```

and for switching
```bash
...
hyprctl bind SUPER,1,workspace,work.ide
hyprctl bind SUPER,2,workspace,work.web
hyprctl unbind SUPER,3
```
3. (optional eye-candy) animation for switching workspaces :
```i think i've seen it in todolist already```

No hurry, no push, just suggestion.
Waiting for feedback

Thank you!

title: hyprctl batch
body:

suggesting to add ability to bypass multiple commands in one `hyprctl` call

 from:
```bash
hyprctl keyword unbind SUPER,q
hyprctl keyword unbind SUPER,w
hyprctl dispatch exec script-name.sh
```
to, like:
```bash
hyprctl < "
(keyword unbind SUPER,q)
(keyword unbind SUPER,w)
(dispatch exec script-name.sh)
" 

(or maybe piping string into hyprctl)
```

Thank you!

title: Hyprctrl: Use printf format specifiers for the usage string
body:
# Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Adds format specifiers to `printf` in Hyprctl, otherwise Hyprland doesn't compile on my system due to `-Werror=format-security`:

```bash
./main.cpp:135:15: error: format not a string literal and no format arguments [-Werror=format-security]
  135 |         printf(USAGE.c_str());
```

It's good practice to always include format specifiers anyways, even though this does not revolve around user input

# Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

No

# Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Yes

title: Crash: Underflow in removeBeginEndSpacesTabs(): Assertion '__pos <= size()' failed.
body:
**Describe the bug** After compiling the latest commit of Hyprland on my system and trying to start it, Hyprland crashes with the following message: `/usr/include/c++/12.1.0/bits/basic_string.h:1221: constexpr std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::reference std::__cxx11::basic_string<_CharT, _Traits, _Alloc>::operator[](size_type) [with _CharT = char; _Traits = std::char_traits; _Alloc = std::allocator; reference = char&; size_type = long unsigned int]: Assertion '__pos <= size()' failed.` This happens both with the auto-generated config file and the example provided in the repository. After running it through gdb, the following loop in the `removeBeginEndSpacesTabs()` function seems to be the issue: ```cxx while (str[str.length() - 1] == ' ' || str[str.length() - 1] == '\t') { str = str.substr(0, str.length() - 1); } ``` It looks like `substr()` is underflowing here (the value of `__pos` is `numeric_limits(size_t)::max()`: ```gdb in std::__cxx11::basic_string, std::allocator >::operator[](unsigned long) (__pos=18446744073709551615, this=0x7fff697f9370) at /usr/include/c++/12.1.0/bits/basic_string.h:1221 ``` **Images/videos/anything that would help**

title: Nix: more tweaks to the flake
body:
Hello, I made some changes to the flake.nix to further comply with the ecosystem.
Before anything, I want to discuss it with the previous contributors of the flake (pinging @Narice @Tanish2002  #78 )
- `packages`: changed the output to `default`, which is the new default target instead of `#defaultPackage.<system>`. I also added an output for the custom wlroots build, in case some builds fail in the future.
- `apps`: the latest versions of nix automatically convert `packages` to `apps` by using the attribute `meta.mainProgram`, and it picks up `packages.<system>.default` or `apps.<system>.default`. So this output is not needed anymore.
- `inputs`: I removed FU (bloat). `nixpkgs-wayland`'s wlroots was just `nixpkgs`'s wlroots with an overriden `src`, which is exactly what we do in `packages.<system>.wlroots`, so I removed it too. The `nixpkgs` input has been changed to `nixos-unstable`, which I find more reasonable, given the nature of the software.
- `formatters`: a recently added output, which formats all nix files just by running `nix fmt`. I chose `alejandra` as the formatter (and formatted all the nixfiles with it), as I find that it produces the most diff-friendly code. Open to discussion...
- `overlay`: initially I wanted to entirely remove this output, but decided to keep it to not break people's setups. With such a simple flake layout, the downstream consumers can just use `(inputs).Hyprland.packages.x86_64-linux.default`, instead of adding the overlay, and then `pkgs.hyprland`. Overlays are cumbersome to use, compose, and introduce some other problems (read https://zimbatm.com/notes/1000-instances-of-nixpkgs ).

Following this, the wiki should be updated to include information for installation without overlays.

I also added a GitHub Workflow that automatically builds the package, in parallel with the Arch build. You can see it in action here: https://github.com/viperML/Hyprland/actions/runs/2338469084 . Ideally, another GH action would be needed to bump the `flake.lock` on schedule (weekly maybe?)

title: Move cursor to corner of focused window
body:
**Describe in detail your idea.**

I noticed that when movefocus is called the cursor moves to the center of the focused window.
In xmonad there is a way to move the cursor to the corners of the screen by pressing a key combination

Here is one way I used the feature when I was using xmonad
https://github.com/japrogramer/xmonad-hs/blob/master/xmonad.hs#L156

title: Submap of key bindings
body:
**Describe in detail your idea.**

In Xmonad it is possible to have nested key combinations.

https://xmonad.github.io/xmonad-docs/xmonad-contrib/XMonad-Actions-Submap.html

title: nix: update workflow and bump flake
body:
Addresses the conversation in #86 

This PR adds an flake update action, so the `flake.lock` is not left for days without update.
This action can be manually triggered to update the dependencies (and the wlroots build) to their latest versions.

The timer is set to run every 2 weeks, which seems reasonable.

title: Implement moveCurrentWorkspaceToMonitor,(number|next|previous)
body:
**Describe in detail your idea.**

As it says above. Multi-monitor support is where tilling WM shine. Having the ability of move entire workspaces around from monitor to monitor is a core feature of multi-monitor support.

Detail: 
moveCurrentWorkspaceToMonitor,(number|next|previous) would obviously move an entire workspace to a different monitor specified by its number, or previous or next

There's actually probably two variants of this that could benefit from being implemented:
- moveCurrentWorkspaceToMonitor,monitor_number (or previous or next)
- moveWorkspaceToMonitor,Workspace_number,Monitor_number (or previous or next)

:-)

- **if there is however, then** :

  (b) clients in this pre-existing WS are moved to the new WS on the external monitor (but they are mislocated on it, see below)

The windows are "mislocated" as they appears on the left, superimposed, and can't be dragged/moved etc

I hope that helps!

title: Focus next WS on monitor
body:
Last one for a while, I promise.

When using multiple monitors, one often wants to navigate the WS on the current monitor only, and keep the other monitor focused on the same WS. With the current implementation of "workspace,+1 | -1", I am going through all WS in order, and thus potentially changing the WS on the other monitor if I go through WS on it. Of course, I can use "workspace,N" directly, but for my workflow I am used to next/previous WS (which means I don't have to reach up to the number keys and think it over, arrow keys are a shorter reach).

This would be done by implementing a "focusNextWSonCurrentMonitor" (or prev). Of course, that would mean to keep a registry of what WS are on what monitor, but you probably have that already :-)

**Alternatively and probably a better idea** than a separate command, 
```bash
workspace,nextOnMonitor | prevOnMonitor
```
might be better.

An extension of this for a move:
```bash
movetoworkspace,nextOnMonitor | prevOnMonitor
```
would also be very useful

All this would not break the current behaviour, just add a very useful functionality.

title: Hardcoded /tmp/hypr problematic
body:
Hi,

this looks like an interesting project.

While looking at the code I noticed that the hardcoded paths `/tmp/hypr/hyprland.log` and `/tmp/hypr/.socket.sock` which will break if more than one instance of hyprland is running.

I would suggest making use of the XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and WAYLAND_DISPLAY environment variables for the socket file. Eg replace using `/tmp/hyper/` with `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/${WAYLAND_DISPLAY}-hypr/`.

This location should be fine for the socket, but strictly speaking, log files shouldn't go under ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}. However, I'm guessing that the currently implemented logging will be changed as hyprland becomes more mature. Is there any reason not to use `wlr_log()` provided by wlroots?

Cheers,

Nick.

title: How to handle lid switching ?
body:
Hi,

I'm trying to auto turn off my laptop's screen when i close the lid, I have tried with `elogind`, but it doesn't seem to works. With wayland we can use `bindswitch` command but it seems there is nothing like that in Hyprland. 

Is there a keyword or anything like that undocumented ?

title: Allow hyprctl to move/resize windows to specific values (not delta) for floating windows
body:
Hello! 

I have a suggestions.  It would be nice to use `hyprctl` to be able to move floating windows to discrete locations rather than using the current "pixel delta" actions.  I use an ultrawide monitor which makes the first window in a tiling algo comically large.  so i prefer to stay in a "floating" layout but arrange them in configurations that work with the ultrawide monitor.  i want to setup keybinds that can move the current window to specific x,y,w,h coordinates.

title: Link errors when building without xwayland
body: Attempting to build Hyprland when wlroots does not have xwayland support enabled results in linker errors even when `-DNO_XWAYLAND=true` is set. I would expect that setting that flag completely ifdefs out the XWayland code but it doesn't. As it currently stands even if you try to disable XWayland support in hyprland you must have wlroots built with XWayland support and therefore you must have the xwayland dependencies installed even if you do not wish to use them.

title: SuperShift+BackTab binding not working
body:
### Steps to reproduce

In my i3 and sway config, I like to use meta+Tab and meta+BackSpace to walk through workspaces, adding shift to reverse their behaviour. Here's the lines in my hyprland.conf:

```
bind=SUPER,tab,workspace,m+1
bind=SUPER,backspace,workspace,m-1
bind=SUPERSHIFT,backspace,workspace,m+1
bind=SUPERSHIFT,tab,workspace,m-1
bind=SUPERSHIFT,backtab,workspace,m-1
```
### Expected Outcome

Super+Shift+Tab ought to do what it's configured to.

### Noted Outcome

I seems the last two lines don't work, and they don't produce an error message. I tried backtab on the suggestion of the FAQ.

### Extra info

Running Hyprland v0.4.0beta on OpenSuSE Leap 5.18-1-1 default on a ThinkPad L14 Gen 1.

title: Natural scrolling for touchpad only
body: With <https://github.com/vaxerski/Hyprland/issues/63>, natural scrolling was implemented. However, the setting makes it so that both mouse and touchpad have reverse scrolling, which is undesirable by most people. Would it be possible to implement natural scrolling that only affects the touchpad? Thank you.

title: fullscreen fix
body: Fix according to your suggestion, tested and ready to merge.

title: Add natural_scrolling option for touchpads only
body: This PR makes the existing `input:natural_scroll` setting affect only the mouse, and adds a separate `input:touchpad:natural_scroll` for touchpads.

title: Add loose follow_mouse option
body: Allows the `follow_mouse` config option to be set to 2, which makes it so that moving the cursor doesn't focus windows, but still calls `notify_enter` so that the windows interact with the cursor correctly (such as for scrolling and hover effects). Keyboard events like typing and navigation still occur in the focused window. Tested and works on Arch.

title: Add movewindowinv dispatcher
body:
Adds the `movewindowinv` dispatcher, which is similar to `movewindow` but moves all windows within the active workspace _except_ the active window (and takes only a monitor as its argument). Useful for when you want to quickly give space to particular window. 

This also moves most of the code from the `moveActiveToWorkspace` method into a new method so that it can be used by the new dispatcher. I've tested both the `movewindowinv` dispatcher and the affected `movewindow` dispatcher.

Example config:
```
bind=SUPER,left,movewindowinv,l
bind=SUPER,right,movewindowinv,r
```

 
Demo video using the above config (I couldn't get the second monitor to be recorded, but that's where the windows are going):

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44363049/173507834-f6742ead-b32b-4622-801f-e3a143ea57e3.mp4

title: Added meson buildfiles
body:
this makes for a far better experience in combination with wlroots,
since that whole makefile mess is not required.
Additionally, handling of wayland protocol sources is also slightly
better, but could be improved with mesons inbuilt wayland module.

To build Hyprland using meson:
```
meson _build -Ddefault_library=static
ninja -C _build
ninja -C _build install
```

Some code is taken from sway and wlroots.

title: Don't use sudo in the makefile
body:
`cd wlroots && sudo ninja -C build/ install`
Making use of `sudo` to install the package should not be required. In the case of Archlinux's `makepkg`, we don't need these rights to properly finish the packaging process. Furthermore, this breaks automated builds in clean chroots which don't have a superuser set up.

**Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?**

I also noticed that angular camera movement was also weird, and that's fixed too, but that might just be because I changed from accelerated mouse movement to forced linear. 


**Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)**
This obviously locks the cursor to the center of the screen while constrained, so if this breaks some workflow I'm not aware of, please let me know. This was created to play games better, and that's what it successfully does.

title: [Feature Request] Runtime configuration options?
body:
WMs like bspwm or [hlwm](https://herbstluftwm.org/herbstluftwm.html) exposes everything for the configuration into shell (from sockets). This makes it easy to test out changes when windows are opened and things are running.

Hlwm also offers a locking mechanism where if the hlwm is started with `--locked`, all the style changes are deferred until `hc unlock` is called. That way default themes are not applied and after everything is queued, things start drawing. Can also manually lock and unlock with `hc lock` and `hc unlock` in case we want to do multiple changes and stay responsive/efficient while doing so, as sockets have latency (e.g. switching light/dark mode of multiple things borders / bg / frame / etc).

How cool would it be if we're able to configure & test out stuffs at runtime (with `hyprctl` which already allows socket talking as I see), without exiting the session or try to run different wm in another tty, and get the results seen in-eye at the exact moment.

title: Cursor does not render
body:
Hi,

The mouse initializes in the upper left corner, and then on either moving the mouse, or launching a window it totally disappears. The mouse still interacts with the screen, I just can't see it! I tried changing the cursor icon (which worked), but I had the same problem.

I'm using the hyprland flake directly with NixOS, pinned at 0.62. I will upload the logs soon as I figure out how to do that with a non-visible mouse.....

I didn't have this issue before using nvidia drivers? But I wasn't able to roll back to a point where it did work.

title: Changed dispatcher: focusWindowByClass -> focusWindow. Now supports titles & classes
body:
**Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?**
Before, you could only focus a window by a class and not differentiate ones of the same class. Now you can use a the title keyword, the same way as with window rules. 
title: `focuswindow title:^(.*)(WaniKani)(.*)$`
class: `focuswindow dolphin`

This is useful to, for example, sort multiple auto-launching browser windows to the right workspace. (I use it together with BroTab for Firefox to activate the right pinned tab beforehand)


**Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)**
focusWindow is backwards compatible to focusWindowByClass. So even though I removed it, I kept a dispatcher for focuswindowbyclass -> focusWindow to not break existing configs. 


**Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?**
ready

title: Ability to interact with unfocused windows with a mouse
body:
Currently if a window is outside of focus then we cannot do some actions like scrolling on a window, which do not require the window to be in focus. Instead all those actions are interpreted by the window in focus, this leads to a very confusing behavior.

One method is to enable `follow_mouse` but that also has its own caveats, like the focus being all over the place when navigating with the mouse.

If there could exist any method do some mouse actions on a window without actually bringing it into focus, then any such inconvenience could be resolved.

I hope you'll look into it.

title: Draft: Add 1:1 swipe gestures to switch workspaces
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
I wrote this to enable one-to-one touchpad gestures to switch workspaces as it is a really nice feature to have on laptops.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
I have not tested this with multiple monitors, but presumably it should work fine as it uses the same animations as normal workspace switching.
The gesture is broken if you try to switch between two workspaces that skip an ID, such as going from 3->5. This would have to be fixed before merging.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
No: the bug described above needs to be fixed, and this needs testing under more configs than my own. It would also be a good idea to make this feature configurable (number of fingers, on/off, sensitivity).
Additionally, I left some comments marked TODO which indicate bits of code that, though functional, might need rethinking.

# Description

# Wallpaper
exec-once=hyprpaper

title: Incorrect fullscreen event data in socket2
body:
If you use fullscreen with parameter '1' (keep gaps and bars), this sends an incorrect event through socket2. It will always send the event fullscreen>>0, regardless of if you enter or exit fullscreen. The event works correctly for the other version of fullscreen, the 'true' fullscreen.

I am using this command to test it:
`socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/hypr/$(echo $HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE)/.socket2.sock | while read line; do echo $line; done`

title: Add switching to previous workspace
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Add the ability to switch to the last visited workspace as described in #324, inspired by i3. The syntax suggested in the issue has been adopted: `bind=MODIFIER,KEY,workspace,previous`.

Also included is a toggle setting `general:auto_back_and_forth` to allow switching back to the previous workspace by trying to switch to the same workspace again. I use it all the time in sway and my workflow would be _greatly_ improved by the ability to quickly switch to and from a workspace to check on email, discord, spotify, etc. 
E.g. start in workspace 1, then `Super+7` to workspace 7, and then `Super+7` again will move to workspace 1. 

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
I've moved a lot of code from `CKeybindManager::changeworkspace` to `CCompositor::changeWorkspace`, to make it easier to reuse the raw workspace switching.

This is also my first pull request, so my apologies if I've broken any conventions, just let me know and I'll fix it. I'm also not super experienced with C++, but I think I worked out enough for this small change.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Yes it's ready as far as I know (it builds and works in debug mode). However:

- I'm not sure if I've put `m_bAutoBackAndForth` in the right place - let me know if there's somewhere else for settings like that to go.
- Not sure if some hyprctl commands need to be added too.
- Of course wiki updates will be necessary too, but I don't know how that's normally done.

title: Option to toggle off borders/gaps when there is only 1 window in workspace
body:
There is a feature that I really liked in bspwm that allows you to automatically toggle off borders and gaps when there is only 1 window in the workspace (basically an 'auto-maximize'). I like this feature because I believe gaps are only necessary when there is more than 1 window, so you can easily distinguish them apart. When there is only 1 window, I don't want any gaps so I can dedicate the whole screen to that window.

If this is possible with a script, I would like to know about it. But as I understand, you would have to be checking the current workspace's number of windows, and to get that data you would have to be constantly running awk or something to extract it from the info produced by hyprctl? Just seems really messy and inefficient.

title: VRAM Memory Leak on window close
body:
* Steps to reproduce
   * Launch terminal with `watch -n 1 -d nvidia-smi`
   * Launch 2 new kitty instances (or any other terminal) and then close them
* Expected outcome
   * The VRAM usage should decrease after closing the instances
* Noted outcome
   * The VRAM usage instead increases, this happens until your GPU runs out of VRAM, freezes and you have to kill Hyprland for it to release the memory.

While I know NVIDIA support isn't directly there, it's more a question for how to properly fix this as I don't use Discord. A reset was also performed, without making any difference.
Tried `nvidia-open`, `nvidia` and `nvidia-lts` drivers (both DKMS and non), all ending in the same memory leak.

Env:
```
export CLUTTER_BACKEND=wayland
export XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland
export QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland
export QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_WINDOWDECORATION=1
export MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1
export GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm
export __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia
export WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS=1
```

nvidia-smi:
Before opening 2 instances:
`0   N/A  N/A       918      G   Hyprland                          294MiB`
After opening and closing 2 instances:
`0   N/A  N/A       918      G   Hyprland                          314MiB`

I've also tried to disable things like blur, which also didn't reduce the leaks. This is using the standard-generated config with changed keybindings and `exec-once=dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` added at the bottom.

title: Hyprland ignores kb_variant after switching layouts.
body:
In my Hyprland config, I have the following lines for input settings and changing layouts:

```
input {
    kb_layout=us,ru
    kb_variant=workman,
    kb_model=
    kb_options=caps:escape
    kb_rules=

    follow_mouse=1
    force_no_accel=true
}

bind=SUPER,space,exec,hyprctl keyword input:kb_layout ru
bind=SUPER,space,exec,hyprctl keyword input:kb_layout us
```
As you can see in the config, my `kb_variant` is set to `workman,`. But when i change layout to `ru`, and then change it back to `us`, Hyprland ignores the `kb_variant` option and sets my layout variant to qwerty.

### Steps to reproduce:
1. Embed lines from above in Hyprland config.
2. Press Super + Space to change layout to `ru`.
3. Press Super + Space again to change layout back to `us`.

### Expected outcome:
Hyprland should change layout to `us` with **workman** variant.

### Noted outcome:
Hyprland changes the layout to `us` with **qwerty** variant.

title: New floating windows are not interactive if they appear above maximized windows.
body:
Steps to reproduce:
- Maximize a windowed program such as Firefox.
- Have the program open a new floating window while maximized. (For instance open a page in Firefox which downloads a file. Firefox will then open a floating window asking what it should do with the corresponding file.)
- The new floating window is visible in front of the maximized tiled window. But is not interactive unless the maximized program is no longer maximized or the floating window is moved to a sepperate workspace.

Expected outcome:
The new floating window is interactive on top of the maximized tiled window.

OS: Gentoo Linux x64 5.15.41
Hyprland version: 0.7.1beta

title: docs: add man pages
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
This PR adds a man page for both `Hyprland` and `hyprctl`.

The man pages are written in `.rst` format so it is easy to read and edit.

`rst2man` is used during install to convert the pages. They are then piped into `gzip` for compression and finally written to the proper man directory.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
There should be no bugs added as there is no code changed except for the two lines added into the Makefile.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
This is ready to be merged afaik.

The man pages can be extended later to include a `Hyprland-conf.5` page for configurations.

Let me know of anything you would change. I have built and tested using the cmake method from the documentation.

To test the man pages you do not need to build the whole program. You can use `rst2man ./docs/hyprctl.1.rst | man -l -`

`python-docutils` for Arch should probably be added as a build dependency in the wiki when this is merged.

Adds the option to focuswindow by pid and address (as can be found by using hyprctl) by specifying "pid:" or "address:". Helpful for creating scripts where you want to focus a specific window.

title: nix: add home-manager module

Hey, folks!

### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Adds a [home-manager](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager) module.

I built this module for my own use a few weeks ago, so I decided to polish it up and upstream it :)

For those uninitiated with nix: home-manager has modules (abstractions) for doing things on the user (instead of system, as is for NixOS modules) level. It has a lot more (and more extensive) modules than NixOS when we're talking about "dotfiley" stuff (editors, window-managers, terminals, etc).

[Some example usage on my config repo](https://github.com/Misterio77/nix-config/blob/d19cf7ae7d47d1b9ee7ed7521efa16f64f1d886c/home/misterio/desktop/hyprland/default.nix#L8)

title: [Master Stack] Support multiple windows in master pane of master/stack layout
body:

Supporting this in Hyprland would require adding two extra commands: one to increment and one to decrement the count (or one command with a parameter). If the count goes to zero, the left pane vanishes and is replaced by an expanded stack.

title: unlock the event queue before sleeping
body:
I'm seeing weird ordering of events over the socket, I think it's because the event queue mutex is held while it sleeps. It just continues after waking up, so it can be unlocked before sleep.

For example, flipping through the workspaces:

```
$ hsock | grep "^workspace"
workspace>>3
workspace>>2
workspace>>5
workspace>>4
workspace>>6
workspace>>7
workspace>>8
workspace>>10
workspace>>9
```

Same thing but unlocking before sleep:

```
$ hsock | grep "^workspace"
workspace>>2
workspace>>3
workspace>>4
workspace>>5
workspace>>6
workspace>>7
workspace>>8
workspace>>9
workspace>>10
```

title: SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode not capturing the mouse
body:
In SDL, running `SDL_SetRelativeMouseMode(SDL_TRUE)` under the Wayland backend should hide the mouse cursor and lock it to that window, to be used in camera controls in games for example. In Hyprland, this function only hides the cursor, but it can still freely move out of the window and thus breaks games using it.

I have verified the function works as intended in Sway.

The function's source: https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/main/src/video/wayland/SDL_waylandmouse.c#L541
https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/bdaf9a92a661debd6b31d82421ffdfa202b8ae72/src/video/wayland/SDL_waylandevents.c#L2298

I can provide a test binary if helpful.

title: Monitor Cycling
body:
Though this can be somewhat hacked around, it would be nice to have a relative ID option for monitor selection in the configuration identical to how workspaces function. Seems like it would make the configuration feel a little more consistent between monitors and workspaces.

This way it would be fairly trivial to configure a single keybind for cycling through monitors, or in the case of two monitors, swapping between the two. 

Alternatively, if the direction for monitors cycled back around, such that going right on the right most monitor would go leftmost, it would make a similar setup also trivial. But that feels like it would break existing configurations and/or cause more unintended consequences.

title: Add window{open/close/move} IPC events
body:
I am making a custom status bar using the `eww` framework. And I need to know when windows open, close and move between workspaces.

Open/close is pretty straightforward. I tried to emit IPC events in `Events::listener_mapWindow`/`Events::listener_unmapWindow` and it worked fine. 

Move, on the other hand, is tricky, because `CWindow.m_iWorkspaceID` is public and is being changed all over the place. There are at least 3 places where I need to emit the "move" IPC event:
1. Move window via keybind
2. Drag window and switch workspace
3. Pick window, switch workspace and drop it (without mouse movement)

I suggest hiding `CWindow.m_iWorkspaceID` behind getter/setter. Then it will be possible to emit the event just in the setter.

Would you be willing to merge that?

title: New windows in inactive workspaces stealing focus
body:
To reproduce:
One way is to first make sure you have a window rule assigning whatever browser you use to a specific workspace. I have these rules:
```
windowrule = workspace 1 silent,^(librewolf)$
windowrule = workspace 1 silent,^(firefox)$
```
Then you can go to [this page](https://www.bennish.net/web-notifications.html), give it permission to display notifications, then click show in 5s. Switch to a fullscreen window in a different workspace, wait the 5 seconds for the notification window to open, and the active window will then be un-fullscreened.

Another way is by opening a terminal window and running something like this:
```sh
sleep 5; pavucontrol
```
And then again, switch to a fullscreen window in any workspace other than the one to which pavucontrol (or whatever program you choose to run) is assigned.
I have this window rule:
```
windowrule = workspace 4 silent,^(pavucontrol)$
```

Expected behavior:
If a workspace windowrule contains `silent` then matching windows should not get focus, unless that window's workspace is already the active one.

Actual behavior:
If the new window is in the same workspace as the focused one, that new window gets focus and the previous one does not get it back. I would say that's pretty normal behavior. When the new window opens in a different workspace, it seems to steal it momentarily and then give it right back to the previously focused window. The previously focused window regains focus whether `follow_mouse` is enabled or disabled.

I'm running both Hyprland and wlroots built from source, cloned less than an hour before posting this issue so I'm up to date.

title: Addressing deficiencies in documentation
body:
Some of the documentation is insufficient, wrong, or confusing. I will edit this issue as I come across things that I have questions about. The more questions your documentation answers, the less people bother you.

- [ ] What is [psuedotile](https://wiki.hyprland.org/Configuring/Dwindle-Layout/#config)? I can see what it does, but what is the purpose? If there were a description, I would know that it is working correctly.
  - Firefox, when in a tall tile on half of the screen, does not appear to do anything with psuedotiling mode.
  - Even with `dwindle.psuedotile` set to `false`, I can still make a bind using the `psuedo` dispatcher. How does the option interact with the bind dispatcher, and what is it supposed to do if not disable the dispatcher?
- [ ] What is [clickfinger](https://wiki.hyprland.org/Configuring/Basic-Config/#touchpad) and how does it behave?
- [ ] How does [middle button emulation](https://wiki.hyprland.org/Configuring/Basic-Config/#touchpad) work? Is it a three-finger tap? Isn't that a part of `tap-to-click`?
  - Why does `middle_button_emulation` change nothing when set to `false` (under the assumption that it is supposed to be three-finger tap)?
  - Why does `tap-to-click` have a hyphenated name versus everything else which is underscored? How does it interact with "clickfinger" and "middle button emulation"?

title: Streamline dwindle groups
body:
### Definition

I had a look into the implementation of dwindle groups. For a clean design and rigorous implementation, I would propose the following definition:

> For each tiling window, we have a **terminal** node (i.e. no further children) , to which the window is assigned to. A **group** is a non-terminal node in the dwindle tree, that exposes the window of one of its descendant terminal nodes (selectable),  solely, on the entire viewport of the group . Normal non-terminal nodes, in short **nodes**, don't do that and just distribute the remaining rendering space to its children.


### Implementation guidelines
Implementation wise this can be achieved when sticking to the following principles:
* Always keep the binary tree intact. Even with a group being present, they behave transparent with regard to the tree: Nodes/child nodes are handled (moved, resized, inserted, etc.) completely normal (like in case of a plain node) 
* A grouping action is just a matter of visualization and does not affect the tree structure: If a node turns into a group, it short-cuts the window rendering at this tree position and presents a window of it descendant child nodes.

### Development state
In this PR, I implemented the outlined behavior to provide a proof of concept. It was easiest to discard the most recent changes w.r.t groups in the main branch (in particular c319a2aba9cf993d26af7af66a8632aad6a83d1b) and give it a fresh start.

Apart from a cleaner implementation, we gain the following:
* Grouped nodes remember their original split-ratio when being ungrouped again
* Groups of groups are possible now. Following the definition from above, an outer group still presents **all** reachable child windows. But if the outer group gets dissolved, the inner group becomes visible again.

#### Demo:
The following video:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14107889/187093674-78678dcd-f4bd-48f5-9ac8-b2f2be38fb7f.mp4

 demonstrates the new features. It is driven by the playbook below:
```
#!/bin/zsh

alias D="hyprctl dispatch"
alias S="sleep"

for i in `seq 3`; do 
	S 0.5; D exec ~/.config/hypr/kitty-with-banner;
done

S 1; D resizeactive 120 120
S 2; D togglegroup 1
S 1; D focuswindow "title:.*001$"
S 1; D togglegroup 1
S 2; D togglegroup 0
S 1; D movewindow l
S 1; D focuswindow "title:.*003$"
S 1; D resizeactive -120 0
S 2; D togglegroup 0
S 1; D resizeactive 0 -120
S 1; D movewindow l
```

#### Unresolved issues:
Atm, a few things still need to be done:
- [ ] Fullscreen requests are not handled probably. However, with the concept from above, maximized fullscreen windows can be represented with the top node turned into a group and the view being rotated to the desired window.
- [ ] I did not care about decorations (Don't now how they work). Once this gets fixed, I would suggest to 
    - [ ] use dedicated decoration colors for fullscreen windows, making them easier to identify 

----

I submit this PR to trigger a discussion and get some feedback although the implementation is not finished and thoroughly tested. 
I also do not now how much time I can invest into this within the next week, so help with the remaining issues would be appreciated. But imho, it would be worth it!

title: /tmp/hypr is only accessible by one user
body:
So I have two user on my system, let's say `user1` and  `user2`. I usually run Hyprland with `user1`, and recently I wanted to experiment with Hyprland with `user2`, which I use for gaming. I logged in into Hyprland as `user2` and run `hyprctl clients` or whatever, and receives this error

`Couldn't connect to /tmp/hypr/_1662993714/.socket.sock. (3)`

Basically, the socket file didn't exist. Or rather, the directory that's supposed to contain the socket file didn't exist. no socket, no log file, nothing. 

```
$ ls /tmp/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE
ls: cannot access '/tmp/hypr/_1662993714/.socket.sock': No such file or directory
```

The symptom is similar to #642 , but most likely it was from another cause so I'm opening a new issue.

After investigating for a bit, I found out that `/tmp/hypr` is owned by `user1`, and `user2` could not write into the folder, thus explaining why the socket in `user2`'s session didn't exist.

Apparently Hyprland creates `/tmp/hypr` directory on behalf of `user1` (which is the first to run Hyprland and own `/tmp/hypr) and just assume that everyone can write to `tmp/hypr`.

I can think of several solutions:
- Append user identifier to `/tmp/hypr` directory name, such as `/tmp/hypr-user1` or something. This way each user have their own directory that they can write into. One caveat is this will break compatibility with practically every script that connect to Hyprland socket.
- Make `/tmp/hypr` writable by everyone. I don't think this is the best solution, security wise.

title: Disable togglegroup in fullscreen
body:
Given there are multiple windows on one workspace and one of them is shown fullscreen.
It's quite confusing to use togglegroup from that fullscreen state because it's not visible at that moment which windows are children of the visible window.
The only way to know would be to memorize it, and i don't think that would be very common.
A group that contains all windows on a workspace looks the same as a fullscreen window, but the behaviour of togglegroup is completely different and it's nessesary to be able to toggle that group. 
I think a reasonable solution would be to disable togglegroup if a fullscreen window is shown, and maybe even disable fullscreen if a group spans the full screen anyways.

title: Pinned windows in combination with fullscreen
body:
With a pinned floating window, and a fullscreen window on the active workspace,
if you movefocus to the pinned window, it fullscreens.
While it is nice to be able to fullscreen a pinned window sometimes, 
the automatic fullscreening when moving to the pinned window is unintuitive (at least for me).
I'm not totally shure how i would approach this.
One possible sulution would be to treat fullscreen calls different for pinned windows, so that a focused pinned window will fullscreen by the fullscreen command, but not by moving the focus to that window on a fullscreen-workspace.
It would be sad to lose the ability to fullscreen a pinned window, so that  unpinning, fullscreening, unfullscreening, pinning again would be nessesary for quickly having a broader look inside that window.
There could be other maybe better solutions, i just think the actual behavior is confusing.
Switching to another workspace with a pinned fullscreen window is very confusing aswell.

title: Add "highest" mode to Monitor for autoconfiguration.
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Adds 2 new monitor resolution modes.
-- highrr -> highest with refreshrate preference
-- highres -> highest with resolution preference

Should none be possible for whatever reason, then it will default to preferred.

These 2 features are useful to autoconfigure monitors that do not have a good preferred mode. aka 4k monitor defaulting to 1080p or high refreshrate defaulting to 60.
This also means that switching between them is now possible.

this would add a rule for all random monitors to use their "best" possible setting.
monitor=,highrr,auto,1
OR
monitor=,highres,auto,1

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
If someone has wonky setups that can be tested with this, then please do so, it was intended for exactly this.

title: Missing animation for window dimming when using gestures
body:
## Steps to reproduce

- Set `dim_inactive` to true (and set `dim_strength` to a high value to notice it easier)
- enable `workspace_swipe`
- open multiple windows on two workspaces
- swipe towards another workspace with active windows completely without releasing the fingers
- now release the fingers
## Noted outcome
The new active window jumps from a dimmed state straight to the undimmed state, which feels wrong.
## Expected outcome
Either the new active window should already be undimmed when swiping or it should play the fading animation for dimming that is also present when switching focus within a single workspace.
I would personally really like to see a 1:1 dimming strength for the new active window based on the swiping progress but that would probably be more work.

PS: I have just started to use Hyprland on my laptop (sadly with nvidia) today and like it just can't get enough of these gorgeous animations :D

title: Border_size isn't scaling across displays
body:
Steps to reproduce: have 2 displays with 2 different scaling settings, in this case one 4k with 2x scaling and a fhd one with 1x scaling
Expected outcome: general:border_size is costant across different scalings
Noted outcome: on the scale 1 monitor the borders will be two times bigger than on the scale 2 monitor.

It just feels wrong; above all since gaps_out and gaps_in are perfectly synchronized between different displays with different scaling but that doesn't apply to border_size.

title: allow managing desktop lid
body:
I realize I'm missing something big from sway: the ability to handle the laptop LID events.

Sway has a way to bind a switch like so

```
bindswitch --reload --locked lid:toggle exec ~/.bin/lid.sh
```
reload means to rerun the script to align the state on sway reload
locked means it should trigger even if locked
lid:toggle is a handler that will make the binding trigger on change of the LID switch state

This is the first thing I miss from Hyprland (I know logind can handle this, but it sucks and I can't do what I want to do)

Second (maybe I missed it) is to be able to toggle on and off a *single* monitor (with `swaymsg output <name|*> enable|disable`). Hyprland seems to be able to completely disable a monitor (and completely loose track of it until reload) or dpms off all the monitors at once

Here's the content of my lid.sh script

```
#!/bin/env bash

if grep -q open /proc/acpi/button/lid/LID0/state; then
	swaymsg "output eDP-1 enable"
else
	# If we are not in CLAMSHELL mode
	if [[ "$(swaymsg -t get_outputs | grep -c name)" == "1" ]]; then
		suspend.sh force
	else
		swaymsg "output eDP-1 disable"
	fi
fi
```

I don't see any way to replicate any of these in Hyprland

title: Window swallowing doesn't work with multiple windows owned by a single process
body:
If multiple terminal windows are owned by a single process (for example terminals that run in client/server mode), only the first window will actually be swallowed.

### Steps to reproduce:

Open two kitty windows using kitty --single-instance (I've also tested this with foot using foot -s and footclient). Launch MPV (or any other command that spawns a window) in both terminals.

### Expected outcome:

Both windows should be swallowed by their respective commands.

### Noted outcome:

Only the first window is actually swallowed. The second one is not.

### Workaround:

You get the expected behavior however when you use terminals that run as separate processes, but this uses much more system resources and is thus less than ideal.

title: Remove texcoord from QUADFRAGSRC.

QUADFRAGSRC isn't using that variable inside the non rounding code. 
Because of that opengl optimizes that variable out, and is complaining if glGetAttribLocation is called on it.

title: Window Rule for min-size of floating windows
body:
So we currently have the window rule `size [x] [y]` for resizing a floating window on open.
I would really appreciate a rule, let's call it `min-size [x] [y]`, that only resizes a floating window if the spawned window has an initial height and width that is less than `[x] [y]`. 
Same could be done for `max-size` the other way around, although a minimum setting would be enough imo.

title: security: implement ext-session-lock-v1
body:
It seems Hyprland is not implementing ext-session-lock-v1 (https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/131) (implemented in swaylock here https://github.com/swaywm/swaylock/pull/219)

Today if I start swaylock, then switch to another tty and kill it, then come back to Hyprland, I'm back into my session. So basically that means if swaylock crashes, nothing is locked anymore. In Sway, if I do the same, the screen is all red and I can't do anything (the lockscreen is dead, but the session is still locked)

title: weird kill -TERM behavior
body: On Hyprland (and only on Hyprland) kill -TERM has no effect anywhere. This work fine on raw tty or Sway. Could Hyprland trap this somehow?

Ready.

title: monitor transform 90 and 270
body:
In the transition from 0.15.1 from 0.15.0 my third monitor which is rotated 90 degrees did this strange skew thing where some of the outline of the window would shade over the top also the corner would completely disapear but you could still see the cursor.  The way the cursor reacts to the rotation is absolutely correct with all the borders but it seems to be just a visual issue. I tested with my other monitors with 90 and 270 and it did the same thing

title: VRAM and RAM Memory Leak on config reload
body:
## How to reproduce

1. To monitor memory usage open `nvtop` (displays both RAM and VRAM) or run `watch -n 1 -d nvidia-smi` (VRAM only).

2. Run `hyprctl reload` few times

## Expected behavior

VRAM / RAM usage +- stays at the level it was.

## Actual behavior

After about 20 reloads VRAM peaks at about max capacity.
Further reloads don't increase usage, but it never decreases on its own.

Here is how it looks in `nvtop`:

<details>
  <summary>nvtop</summary>

![screenshot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14999778/194642012-5d604be7-b185-46c1-ad48-ae33de7b92f8.png)
![screenshot3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14999778/194642028-c3627eb3-144f-4313-adc3-fc41ec7c288e.png)

</details>

## System

* Arch Linux latest
* linux-zen 5.19.13
* nvidia-dkms 515.76-1 ([Instructions](https://wiki.hyprland.org/Nvidia/) from the wiki applied except fixes for flickering)
* Hyprland 0.15.1beta, generated config + few bindings, nothing fancy

Log, obtained by commenting -> saving -> uncommenting -> saving one option (binding) a bunch of times (I didn't realized then that you can trigger the same behavior with `hyprctl reload`):

title: Add input:touchdevice:transform config

Add support for touch device roation. 

The rotation is set globally with `input:touchdevice:td_rotation` and by device with `td_rotation` in a device block.

#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

When rotating the display of a touch screen, the input from the touch device don't take into acount the roation. This PR allows to set a calibration matrix that rotate the input of a touch device by steeps of 90°.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I'm not sure about how to configure the calibration matrix. I ended up getting an index from the config file to select a matrix from an array of matrices defined in `setTouchDeviceConfigs()`, but there is probably a better way to do it.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

It works on my machine :tm:, but I'm not familiar with this code base, so this needs a good proofreading by someone who is.

The new window is spawned, but the terminal is not swallowed.

title: `workspace,previous` to empty workspace creates nameless workspace
body:
## How to reproduce

Relevant config: `binds:allow_workspace_cycles = 1` and `binds:workspace_back_and_forth = 1`.

1. Let's say you have workspace 1 (occupied) and workspace 2 (occupied).

2. You switch between the two using `workspace,previous`.

3. Now close windows on workspace 2, and run `previous` again - it works as expected.

3. Try to run `previous` yet again - it works, but will look like this in waybar

![13-10-2022-13_32_26](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14999778/195581533-70ece1ee-4d52-495f-8bcc-bc4b8b9d1884.jpg)

...and here how `hyprctl` sees it:

```
❯ hyprctl activewindow
Window 82884b00 -> ~ - zsh:
	at: 0,0
	size: 2560,1396
	workspace: 2 ()
	floating: 0
	monitor: 0
	class: kitty
	title: ~ - zsh
	pid: 104472
	xwayland: 0

❯ hyprctl workspaces
workspace ID 1 (1) on monitor DP-1:
	windows: 2
	hasfullscreen: 0
	lastwindow: 0x839331b0
	lastwindowtitle: hyprland issue.md + (~/clouds/Mega/notes) - NVIM

workspace ID 2 () on monitor DP-1:
	windows: 1
	hasfullscreen: 0
	lastwindow: 0x82884b00
	lastwindowtitle: ~ - zsh
```

Notice it has ID (2, like expected) but no name.

4. Now try to switch from this nameless workspace back to 1 using `previous` - _it does nothing_.

## Expected behavior (imo)

If you were to repeat the same steps but by pressing `1` multiple times (remember: `binds:workspace_back_and_forth = 1`), you would be able to switch between workspaces 1 and 2 just fine how many times you like, and empty workspace 2 would be recreated with appropriate name each time.

I think `previous` should behave similarly.

## Culprit?

https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/170def35d79210f9124cdfd7da563d5d384dcae9/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp#L651-L654

So the `workspaceName` is assigned in back and forth branch, but not in [`previous` branch](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/170def35d79210f9124cdfd7da563d5d384dcae9/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp#L612-L630), but it is used [later](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/170def35d79210f9124cdfd7da563d5d384dcae9/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp#L756) regardless.

So the starting value

https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/170def35d79210f9124cdfd7da563d5d384dcae9/src/managers/KeybindManager.cpp#L597

is used.

title: `float_switch_override_focus` should have higher priority than `follow_mouse`
body:
`input:float_switch_override_focus` should have higher priority than `input:follow_mouse`

For example, I have
```c
input {
    follow_mouse = 2
    float_switch_override_focus = false
}
```

When `follow_mouse` is not `1`, the option `float_switch_override_focus` is useless because it respects the former. Perhaps the latter needs three modes, `0: false`, `1: true`, and `3: ignore`?

Mirror the screen after reconnecting

#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

title: Pointer constraints being immediately removed after creation on native Wayland windows
body:
When a Wayland-native application (in my case, [Looking Glass](https://looking-glass.io/)) attempts to constrain the mouse, the constraint seems to be removed immediately on moving the mouse. Hyprland logs while attempting to reproduce this show the following:
```
[LOG] New mouse constraint at 25006c0
[LOG] Registered signal for owner 25067d0: 25007c8 -> 2506848 (owner: Constraint)
[LOG] Registered signal for owner 25067d0: 25007b8 -> 25067e0 (owner: Constraint)
[LOG] Constraint rechecked: 0, 0 to 1169, 609 for 2450050 (window name: )
[LOG] Registered signal for owner 1e584e0: 2450310 -> 1e58538 (owner: Mouse constraint commit)
[LOG] Constrained mouse to 25006c0
<move mouse here>
[LOG] Callback 1e58560 -> 1e58558, Mouse constraint commit removed.
```

Based on that final log message, it appears to me as if [this call to `unconstrainMouse`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/main/src/managers/input/InputManager.cpp#L78) is being fired before it should, especially since it isn't accompanied by a `[LOG] Unconstrained mouse from <id>` message that I observed when testing similar functionality in Minecraft, which uses XWayland.

Reproduction might be tricky for this one, as Looking Glass requires a whole host of complicated VM and PCI passthrough setup to get working, and I'm unaware of any other Wayland-native apps with similar mouse capturing behaviour. although according to #536, SDL applications seem to be exhibiting similar behaviour, so that could be another way to test this. I'm unaware of any SDL apps that try to grab the pointer off the top of my head though. In any case, reproduction should look something like:

1. Open a Wayland-native application that tries to grab the cursor
2. Try to move the mouse outside of the window

Expected: The mouse cannot be moved outside the window.
Actual: The mouse moves outside the window.

title: Feature request: Keychords
body:
### What are keychords?
Keychords are keybindings that can be chained to one another. A famous example is Emacs’ keybind for opening a file `C-x C-f` (read it as Ctrl-x then Ctrl-f).

### Why keychords?
While simple keybindings are easy to implement and fast to press, their number can become quickly limited on a keyboard, especially when trying to keep things organized. Accidentally hit alt when typing Super+q? Guess your computer will shut down instead of just going to sleep.
While keychords require a bit more hand movements, the amount of assignable keybindings becomes virtually limitless while allowing the user to keep their keybindings organized.

### Additional and implementation ideas
Keybindings could be organized in keymaps which could be accessed by other keybindings. I believe this is how i3 handles their own keychords.

Something I really enjoy from Emacs and StumpWM is their `which-key-mode` showing the current keymap’s keybinds, so we never forget them.

title: Dialog focus/refocus issues with forceinput

There are some focusing/refocusing issues when opening and closing dialogs. The documentation suggests to add `forceinput` for solving the issue where windows would not receive focus in certain situations. However, when windows get closed, the pass the focus to the wrong window.

- Add `windowrule = forceinput, (.+)`

- The dialog is focused
- Close dialog with <kbd>Esc</kbd>
- Chrome is focused instead of VSCode

title: Workspace improvements
body:
I'm running awesomewm currently and been playing around with Hyprland to probably switch to. Here are some workspace suggestions, which I think might be useful to others too.

## 1. Show empty workspaces (waybar)
It would be nice to have empty workspaces shown in waybar too. 

## 2. Styling for active workspace even when the monitor has not the focus (waybar)
As per the waybar documentation, `#workspaces button.active` (hyprland) sets the styling for the active workspace. However, this styling is only applied on the focused monitor, but not on other monitors. Do open/active workspaces of non-focused monitors have a class assigned to it?

## 3. Workspaces per output, aka tags, aka groups

This one leads to a lot of confusion, since not everyone can explain what the actual demand is. But I'll try me best. In short, it's basically how awesomewm handles it.

Let's say I have 4 monitors (DP-1... DP-4) and **n** workspaces  (A, B, C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J,K,L,M,N,O,P,Q).
Now, I'd expect each output to show all 3 workspaces (A, B, C,D,E,F,G,H,I,J,K,L,M,N,O,P,Q). When I configure `bind=SUPER,7,workspace,7` it should switch to **G**, but only on the currently focused monitor.

iirc, there's some mentioning about workspace groups in the wayland specs, but I'm not sure whether it covers this usecase or not.

### 3.1 Partial workaround
For anyone interested, I was able to find a workaround for this specific usecase. 

<details>
<summary>hyprland.conf</summary>

This will bind workspace numbers 11-13 to DP-1, 21-23, to DP-2, ... etc. The numbers are apart by 10, so one can use the numbers 1-0 to switch to the workspaces
```
wsbind=11,DP-1
wsbind=12,DP-1
wsbind=13,DP-1

wsbind=21,DP-2
wsbind=22,DP-2
wsbind=23,DP-2

wsbind=31,HDMI-A-1
wsbind=32,HDMI-A-1
wsbind=33,HDMI-A-1

wsbind=41,DP-3
wsbind=42,DP-3
wsbind=43,DP-3

workspace=DP-1,11
workspace=DP-2,21
workspace=HDMI-A-1,31
workspace=DP-3,41

bind=SUPER,2,exec,~/.local/bin/setworkspace.sh 2

```
</details>

<details>
<summary>setworkspace.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
from=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r '.[] | select(."focused"==true).activeWorkspace.id') # ex: 21
mod=$(( $from%10)) # ex: 1
to=$(($from - $mod + $1)) # ex 21-1+2
hyprctl dispatch workspace $to
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>.config/waybar/config</summary>
This will assign a custom icon/text to the specific workspace numbers

```
"wlr/workspaces": {
        "format": "{icon}",
        "format-icons": {
            "1": "A ",
        "11": "A ",
        "21": "A ",
        "31": "A ",
        "41": "A ",
        "2": "B ",
        "12": "B ",
        "22": "B ",
        "32": "B ",
        "42": "B ",
        "3": "C ",
        "13": "C ",
        "23": "C ",
        "33": "C ",
        "43": "C ",
            "focused": "",
            "default": ""
        },
        "active-only": false
    },
```
</details>

## 4. m+1 seems not to work
`bind=SUPER_SHIFT,l,workspace,m+1` I'd expect it to switch to the next workspace on the current monitor, but it does not. Am I misunderstanding something?

title: Nix HM: `exec-once` in systemd integration does not run properly
body:
Seems to be caused by 0d71767. The backslashes are written to `hyprland.conf`, perhaps unintentionally? Hyprland's configuration file does not seem to have a way to escape characters, so the backslashes do not have any special meaning and are taken literally. Relevant part of the generated config:
```
exec-once=/nix/store/bijbd0r4qarawscxi26x9a3bvlri25cm-dbus-1.14.4/bin/dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd \
  DISPLAY WAYLAND_DISPLAY HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP && \
  systemctl --user start hyprland-session.target
```


Relevant part of the logs show that only the first line is executed, while the lines after are seemingly ignored:
```
[LOG] Config executing WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 DISPLAY=:1 /nix/store/bijbd0r4qarawscxi26x9a3bvlri25cm-dbus-1.14.4/bin/dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd \
[LOG] Process created with pid 4036
```

The only possible fix I see is to generate only a single line for the `exec-once`, rather than splitting into multiple lines.

@fufexan

title: meson: unbreak build with BSD find(1)
body:
According to [POSIX](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/utilities/find.html) *path* argument is not optional. Compare [GNU find(1)](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/find.1.html) with [FreeBSD find(1)](https://man.freebsd.org/find/1).

See also [downstream package](https://freshports.org/x11-wm/hyprland-devel).

title: helpers: implement getPPIDof on BSDs (required for window swallowing)
body:
`/proc` has been removed on DragonFly + OpenBSD and deprecated on FreeBSD + NetBSD. Loosely based on [my Firefox fix](https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/e450502ae19e).

`KERN_PROC_PID` references: ([DragonFly](https://man.dragonflybsd.org/?command=sysctl&section=3), [FreeBSD](https://man.freebsd.org/sysctl/3), [NetBSD](https://man.netbsd.org/sysctl.7), [OpenBSD](https://man.openbsd.org/sysctl.2)).

title: Allow arguments to hyprctl dispatch exec commands.
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
`hyprctl` currently errors when a command with arguments is passed to `hyprctl dispatch exec` (see https://github.com/philj56/tofi/issues/60), e.g.

```sh
hyprctl dispatch exec code-oss --unity-launch
# prints usage info
```

as `hyprctl` tries to parse the argument itself. This PR adds the ability to pass `--` as an option to `hyprctl`, to disable parsing of any later arguments à la `swaymsg` and others:

```sh
hyprctl dispatch exec -- code-oss --unity-launch
# correctly runs `code-oss --unity-launch`
```

title: Add keyboards' leds update on Key/Mod press
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

It fixes an issue with some keyboards that attach a few devices at the same time (e.g. picture attached). When one of the mentioned devices changes its mods/keys state, other same-group keyboards are not aware of this change, hence they won't turn on/off the respective keyboard LEDs.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5362310/201471515-0b8a13ba-821b-481d-8219-198fed9ac330.png)

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

Probably this introduces another bug - other keyboards, which do not have modifiers locked, will show up as having one (because of the whole keyboard list update). The best solution, I suppose, would be to filter out/have a list of same-group keyboards and update LEDs only for them. Or just sync mods with other keyboards.

Gnome's mutter or wayfire (I only took a look at their code of keyboard LEDs sync because they worked for my keyboard) - synchronizes all keyboards' mods/LEDs.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

As a quick fix, maybe yes. However, it all depends on how the member of this team decides. I suppose it would be beneficial to implement so mentioned solution, however, I am still not very familiar with keyboard logic in WLR.

title: Master/Stack layout strange behavior
body:
I've been using the master and stack layout for a while and I've come
across some interesting behavior.  If I open 2 windows in a workspace I
will get a split like so (`X` and `Y` represent the two windows):

```
Workspace 1    Workspace 2

  [ X Y ]        [ - - ]
  [ X Y ]        [ - - ]
```

So far the behavior is correct.  If I then go to a second workspace and
do the same thing, I get the same split there:

```
Workspace 1    Workspace 2

  [ X Y ]        [ X Y ]
  [ X Y ]        [ X Y ]
```

However now if I close window `X` in workspace 2, my windows get totally
screwed up and I am left with this layout:

```
Workspace 1    Workspace 2

  [ X - ]        [ - Y ]
  [ Y - ]        [ - Y ]
```

But the expected splits should be this:

```
Workspace 1    Workspace 2

  [ X Y ]        [ Y Y ]
  [ X Y ]        [ Y Y ]
```

I have also tested this with more workspaces, however it seems that the
only workspaces that get affected are the current workspace where the
master window was closed, and the very next workspace you switch to.

title: Perhaps it is a good idea to have a feature "force Xwayland"
body:
There is a way to force an application to be open in Xwayland. 

In sway, you have to use "env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY _application_"

**Why do we need to force application to open in Xwayland?** -:

The thing is, Xorg is a very matured display protocol therefore many linux application were designed with x11 in mind. Some application are very well written in Xorg, but because Wayland adoption is becoming reality, these developer were also considering to port their application to Wayland, but the thing is, this application on Wayland is still not mature and it preferable to be opened in Xwayland. 

"**Some idea to implement this feature**" -:
Perhaps Hyprland can implement this feature using Windows rule, or by just simply allow itself to work like sway did.

title: Dunst invisible (blurred) when run with `sudo su $SUDO_USER -c`
body: ### X: https://github.com/dunst-project/dunst/issues/1126 I have the following minimal example: ```sh for i in 1 2 3 4; do notify-send "Test $i" -h string:synchronous:disable-keyboard sleep 1 done ``` The notification shown does not replace the old one (as it should according to Dunst, and does work for my other scripts). This is not the case if `notify-send` is run directly by the user. I need to do this because the script's primary function requires superuser, and the script is marked as `NOPASSWD` in `/etc/sudoers`. Using `sudo` inline in the script only for the necessary commands is not an option. What happens instead? The first notification is shown correctly, any after that show up as a blurred rectangle in its place. Here is a video where I first run the script, and then the `notify-send` commands individually, finally I copy and paste a contrived example from snippets of the script to demonstrate the commands should work as expected. Note that for the first 30 seconds or so, I am waiting for the script to finish running. After that I start running things manually. Look in the top-right. Due to having weird raw coordinates on some touchpads it should also be possible to set minimum and maximum thresholds on the trackpad's raw values, thus setting and/or limiting the area used on it (using it totally from edge to edge may also be inconvenient on some laptops). This would imply the existence of a few options in the *input/touchpad* session, such as `touchpad_min_x`, `touchpad_min_y`, `touchpad_max_x`, `touchpad_max_y` to restrict the used range of the trackped as mentioned.

These absolute coordinates should also be able to work together with gestures. I would expect the two-finger up-down swipe to still scroll as normal, despite having absolute coordinates.

Finally, as a bonus `hyprctl` could have an option to display raw values from the touchpad to help with the configuration of the usable range, though this is not necessary because we alreadhy have `evtest` to do that for us.

Unfortunately I am not familiar with hyprland's codebase.

title: apply some rules dynamically when state of window changes
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
When toggling the floating state of a window, some rules that change the appearance of a window did not apply anymore, since rules are only matched when a window is created.
This MR will reevaluate the rules when the floating. pinned and fullscreen state of a window changes, and consider these specific rules that affects the window:
noblur, noborder, noshadow, rounding, opacity, bordercolor.

The MR also adds two additional  rule matching fields:
fullscreen - 0/1
pinned - 0/1

example rules:
windowrulev2 = bordercolor rgb(EE4B55) rgb(880808),fullscreen:1
windowrulev2 = bordercolor rgb(32CD32) rgb(7CFC00),floating:1
windowrulev2 = opacity 0.8 0.8,pinned:1

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
I took a selection of rules that seemed relevant to me to modify based on a window state. If more rules should be added or some removed, this is possible. (opaque, noanim, animation maybe?)

I mainly created this because these rules allow me to have a visual clue if a window is in fullscreen or not.
#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

I tested bordercolor and opacity in combination with fullscreen, pinned and floating and did not see an issue. Since rules are only reevaluated when the state changes, I also do not think there is a noticeable performance impact.

I will update the wiki when approved

title: DPMS on has no effect on latest versions
body:
On some monitors, dpms on does not turn the display on.
@wuyoli mentioned what sounds like the same issue here [#489#issuecomment-1317591810](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/489#issuecomment-1317591810)
## Expected outcome
`hyprctl dispatch dpms off` turns the display off
`hyprctl dispatch dpms on` turns the display back on
## Noted outcome
`hyprctl dispatch dpms off` turns the display off as expected
`hyprctl dispatch dpms on` _does not_ turn the display back on
## Steps to reproduce
**I can only reproduce this on one of my two monitors.**
1. Use v0.18.0beta or the latest git version of Hyprland (installed from the AUR)
    i. When using v0.17.0beta, everything works as expected
2. Run `hyprctl dispatch dpms off && sleep 10 && hyprctl dispatch dpms on`
3. The display will turn off, but not back on after 10 seconds like expected
4. Switch to another TTY and back, turning the display on

title: Master layout: choosing placement of master area
body:
I like using the master layout in hyprland (used to it coming from dwm) and I like the very recent improvement to it (master swap toggle). The only issue I still have is that it's currently not ideal on a (second) vertical/portrait monitor, where the master and slave areas are split vertically, leading to two narrow areas.

A possible solution to solve this and make the master layout more powerful would be if the user could choose (per workspace) where to place the master area. We could envision a `masterplacement` command for the layoutmsg dispatcher The current implementation would correspond to `masterplacement left`, but additionally users could opt for `right` (master right, slaves left split horizontally ), `top` (master top, slaves on bottom split vertically) and `bottom` (master bottom, slaves on top split vertically).

Has some relation with #622, which wasn't deemed feasible in the current implementation; this would address the issue whilst sticking to a single layout. 

I might have a try at implementing this myself if the idea is welcomed...

title: Unified border
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Using negative values for the "gaps_in" parameter already allows the user to create a unified border.
Here is an example config snippet for this case:


```
general {
    gaps_in = -1
    gaps_out = 0
    border_size = 2
}
```

Currently, the windows may be drawn in such an order that the border of the active window may not be displayed correctly.

This pull request ensures the active window is drawn last within the first rendering pass.

Here is an example illustrating the current and new behavior with "#" denoting the border of the active window:
```
Current behavior:      New behavior:
#########+--------+    ##########--------+
#        |        |    #        #        |
#        |        |    #        #        |
#########+--------+    ##########--------+
```

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
Nothing here.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
It is ready for merging.

title: Bugfix unintentional cycling workspace with workspace_swipe
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
This PR solves the issue #1053 by adding a new option `workspace_swipe_left_cycle` to `gestures`.
If the option is enabled, it is possible to swipe left on the 1st workspace to go the the -1 workspace (old behaviour)

`workspace_swipe_left_cycle` is disabled by default (changing the default behaviour) but can be enabled if the user wishes
