title: Performance issues with a high workspace ID open
body:
### What I was doing beforehand:
I was doing some testing to see what the highest workspace possible with Hyprland is. It came up to 2147483647.\
Then, when I was done, I just kept a terminal window open to not close off that workspace.\
But afterwords, the compositor froze when I used certain methods for switching workspaces.

### How to recreate
Doing `hyprctl dispatch workspace e+1` would cause a lag spike, and swiping left/right on trackpad also caused the same lag spice.

Image of bottom showing it uses all resources for a small amount of time (it just shows that only 1 core is being used to process this, but this 1 core is halting the entire wm)
![btm in terminal](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57488297/203316655-4d773b0d-f577-4259-8aeb-929de13b2c8f.png)

#### Extra note
Another thing to note is that there is no lag when switching from any workspace using the trackpad from 1 to the last workspace from the large gap. So in this image I can switch through all the workspaces just fine except for with workspace 10 which lags even when I try to swipe to the left (to get to workspace 5).
![Open workspaces in waybar](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57488297/203317192-c1fb165e-fff5-4e5d-81fe-0f325f18fe6d.png)
The lag also doesn't happen when using the `hyprctl` command to switch manually to that workspace (and the sliding animation plays just fine)

#### Suggestion to fix this
Could there be a list storing all the indexes of the open workspaces, then when switching workspaces you get the ID of the workspace to show by subtracting or adding 1 from the index of the current open index.\
This is because what I think you are doing (I haven't checked the code, so this is just a guess) is going changing workspace ID's until you reach one that has a window open.





This is probably a very low priority as I don't think anyone is going to open up 2147483647 workspaces any time soon, but best to have this report in case someone actually needs that many workspaces for some reason.

title: windowrulev2 not working if title/class is not available at window startup
body:
When the title or class is not available at window startup all rules that are not included in the [dynamic rules](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/95047fb08327c5a9c38e5daa46cc3241a1b69cbe/src/Window.cpp#L379) will not be applied to the window. 

Example `windowrulev2` rule:
```
windowrulev2 = tile,title:^(Spotify)$,xwayland:1,
```

Spotify always start in floating mode because the title is not available at startup (from log):

```
[LOG] Searching for matching rules for  (title: )
```

My workaround for now is to call [`listener_mapWindow`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/95047fb08327c5a9c38e5daa46cc3241a1b69cbe/src/events/Windows.cpp#L46) when `listener_setTitleWindow` is called (See [niki-on-github:Hyprland:fix/xwayland-windowrulev2](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/compare/main...niki-on-github:Hyprland:fix/xwayland-windowrulev2).

title: Pin tiled windows
body:
I know of the feature that enables pinning of floating windows and I'd love to use that for normal tiled windows as well. I've looked at the IPC section in the wiki and this feature could possibly be implemented that way, too. Making it a core feature makes more sense to me though as it's already been done for floating windows, that's why I'm writing this suggestion.

My idea is that a pinned tiled window would stay in the same position across all workspaces on the same monitor. That way I'd be able to switch only parts of the current screen and keep the pinned windows there. The size of the windows wouldn't have to remain the same, just putting them in a similar position and then preserving the layout for the respective workspace would be nice. A pinned window might be in different positions and sizes if you rearrange them in a specific workspace.

Ideally you'd be able to specify that a window should only be pinned to specific workspaces.

title: Add option for retrieving first empty workspace
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

This pull request adds a new option to reference workspaces with: "empty".
It references the first empty workspace, i.e. the workspace with the smallest (positive) workspace ID without any windows.

The new option allows to e.g. focus an empty workspace or move a window to an empty workspace by using something like this:

```
bind = $MOD, $KEY1, workspace, empty
bind = $MOD, $KEY2, movetoworkspace, empty
```

These examples are equivalent to the `ws_empty` and `ws_empty_move` actions in spectrwm.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I will add a pull request for updating the wiki entry soon after.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

It is ready for merging.

Based on #173, and the [workflows directory](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/tree/main/.github/workflows), it looks like hyprland is **not** using any automated methods to publish new releases. title: source tarball top level directory & rename tarball
body:
currently the source tarball provided from github has the top level tarball containing all the files: `Hyprland-0.18beta/`, this should be considered for convenience when extracing a tarball, since one would expect something along the lines of what github makes.

[source-v0.18.0beta.tar.gz](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/releases/download/v0.18.0beta/source-v0.18.0beta.tar.gz) has no top level directory, all the files are in the top level directory, without a root directory.

example: 
github tarball:
```
Hyprland-0.18beta/meson.build
Hyprland-0.18beta/src
...
```
source & binary tarball:
```
meson.build
src
...
```

title: rofi won't be centered
Allow swipe gestures to move to next numbered workspace
body: Currently when swipe gestures for workspace switching are turned on, it moves to m+1 workspace or m-1 workspace depending on swipe direction, i.e. it moves to next or previous available workspace. I would rather want to to move to next numbered workspace: example: I have windows spawned on workspaces 1,2,5; when I am on workspace 2, and swipe to go to right workspaces, it goes to workspace 5 because that is the next available workspace, but I would rather want to go to workspace 3, that is +1 instead of m+1. Maybe this could be implemented via a configuration setting like 'workspace_swipe_numbered'

title: nix: add cmake to devshell and create a "wlroots-ready" devshell
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

- fixes `sh: line 1: cmake: command not found` when running `make debug` by adding `cmake` as a nativeBuildInput.

- adds a `wlroots-ready` devshell which puts wlroots in the devshell so nix compiles it.

title: Ability to switch (not redefine!) keyboard layout via `hyprctl` (like `xkb_switch_layout` in sway)
body:
In sway you can

```
swaymsg input type:keyboard xkb_switch_layout <next|prev|index>
```

From the man page:
```
    input <identifier> xkb_switch_layout <index>|next|prev
    Changes the active keyboard layout to counting from zero or to next or previous layout on the list. If there is no next or previous layout, this command hops to the other end of the list.
    This can be used when multiple layouts are configured with xkb_layout. A list of layouts you can switch between can be obtained with swaymsg -t get_inputs.
```

https://man.archlinux.org/man/sway-input.5.en

### Use case

Described here https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/discussions/915, also would help with scripting https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/1162

Basically, switching layouts with `grp:` toggles is very fast, while _redefining_ them via 

```
hyprctl keyword device:*DEVICE*:kb_layout *layout_you_want*
```
is quite a bit slower (like ~1ms? vs 40ms slower)

while `xkb_switch_layout` is like calling grp toggle from cli in terms of latency.

title: Input: Fix unlock mouse warp
body:
Unconstraining a locked mouse would result in the mouse warping to (0, 0), since wlroots give us these as the current mouse position. This PR adds a rather hacky fix for this by manually storing the last mouse position and warp the cursor upon unlocking

Tested with GLFW and glfwSetInputMode() (For reference, GLFW uses zwp_relative_pointer and zwp_locked_pointer)

Current behavior 
 - Lock cursor at (x,y) with glfwSetInputMode(GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED)
 - Move mouse
 - Unlock mouse with glfwSetInputMode(GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL)
 - Cursor is warped to the topleft of the window (0,0)
 
Behavior with this PR
 - Lock cursor at (x,y) with glfwSetInputMode(GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED)
 - Move mouse
 - Unlock mouse with glfwSetInputMode(GLFW_CURSOR_NORMAL)
 - Cursor is warped back to (x,y)

Unfortunately I'm not that familiar of wlroots so I don't know if (un)constraining a mouse is the only time newConstraint/destroyConstraint is called.  

This PR is ready for merging, though I'm open for suggestions/improvements

title: Implement orientation (placement of master area) for master layout
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

This implements the idea I posted in https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/1059 to make the master layout more friendly for use on vertical monitors. Each workspace now has an `orientation` which states where the master area should be (I opted for the more generic term `orientation` rather than `masterplacement`).  The values can be `left` (default, so nothing changes for existing configurations), `top`, `right` and `bottom`.

For the layoutmsg dispatcher the following commands are added:

* orientationleft
* orientationtop
* orientationright
* orientationbottom
* orientationnext   (cycles clockwise)
* orientationprev  (cycles counter-clockwise)

Here's a screenshot of a vertical monitor using the bottom orientation, with the master area at the bottom, and two slave windows on top:

title: cyclenext/swapnext window ordering doesn't match layout
body:
I normally prefer managing my windows with `cyclenext`+`swapnext`. However, `cyclenext` is counterintuitive and hard to predict. I would expect `cyclenext` to go the the next window in the layout, but it seems to be based on the order windows are opened instead.

This bug is one that doesn't crash Hyprland, but feels like invalid behavior.

### Steps to reproduce
1) Make sure that `cyclenext`/`swapnext` are bound to something.
2) Make sure you are using the master layout.
2) Spawn a couple windows and swap them around.
One reproducible way is to spawn four windows and then issue `swapnext` twice, but any swap that reorders the windows works.

### Expected outcome
Using `cyclenext` in master layout shifts focus in order from the top of the stack to the bottom, and then back to the main window.

### Noted outcome
Using `cyclenext` shifts focus in order from the least recently created window to the most recently created window. `swapnext` cannot actually reorder the windows, just their positions on screen.

title: Inconsistent cursor theme on xwayland applications
body:
I couldn't find any relevant information on the wiki on how to solve this issue so I'm here as a last resort, xwayland apps are defaulting to adwaita cursor theme, this behavior wasn't happening before, I have the xcursor env set up properly and hyprctl set cursor theme in the autostart file, as well as in the default file in .icons folder, the gtk3 and 4 settings.ini files. This behavior on gnome wayland isn't present so I guess it has to do more with hyprland and less with wayland in general.

[here's an example](https://im.ezgif.com/tmp/ezgif-1-b8779f15b5.gif)

title: Master layout: lose or inherit fullscreen on deliberate window switching
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

In the master layout as implemented up to this point, when you have a master window, some slave windows and you fullscreen any of them, the fullscreen status remained on the old window even if  you switch to another window via `cyclenext`,`cycleprev`, `swapmaster`, etc...   This meant you effectively couldn't see the window you switched to, had to switch back and manually toggle off fullscreen again. I consider this a bug (though surprisingly didn't find an open issue about it). This PR fixes it in one of two ways:

1. Simply automatically unset the fullscreen status when explicitly switching away from it, showing you all the tiles again (new default behaviour)
2. Like one, but additionally inherit the fullscreen status by immediately re-setting it on the new window. This requires that a new property `master:inherit_fullscreen` is set. This results in behaviour like 'monocle' layout in other tiling WMs. May also be somewhat related to #516. I think this is also more in line with how the dwindle layout does things, judging the comment in #523.

In some cases (like the new orientating switching), I implemented option 1 as the sole option which made sense, otherwise the result of the action would be invisible.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I introduced two new helper functions `prepareLoseFocus` and `prepareNewFocus` to keep the amount of repetition in the code lower.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Should be ready to go

title: widows moved to special workspace remain focused
body:
Windows that recive `movetoworkspace special` remain focused even tho the focused workspace stays the same, the only way to regain focus is by moving the mouse (or creating another window, the new window will be created on the focused workspace)

Step to reproduce:

1. Use movetoworkspace special on any window
2. Window will remain focused even tho workspace has not changed

What should have happened

- Equivalent to movetoworkspacesilent, window should lose focus 
- Or actual behavior of movetoworkspace, special workspace should be focused

I consider this a bug because when that happens, the only way the take back focus is by moving the mouse (creating another window also works).

title: Previous workspace is forgotten or cycles too far
body:
This applies to when `binds:allow_workspace_cycles` is set to `false`:

The `workspace previous` command is not working as I'd expect.  I'm using the master layout (though the code seems to generically apply to all) and I would expect `workspace previous` always to return to the previous workspace (the one I was on before switching), effectively allowing me to toggle between my last two workspaces indefinitely. Instead, I find that cycling to the previous workspace is no longer possible after I used it once.

observed behaviour:

```
workspace 1 -> ok
workspace 2 -> ok
workspace 3 -> ok
workspace previous -> takes me to 2, ok
workspace previous -> takes me to 1, not ok, I have allow_workspace_cycles disabled
workspace previous -> takes me to 3 (why now?)
workspace previous -> no action, keeps me at 3
.. stuck at 3..
```

expected behaviour:

```
workspace 1
workspace 2
workspace 3
workspace previous -> takes me to 2
workspace previous -> takes me to 3
workspace previous -> takes me to 2
workspace previous -> takes me to 3
..repeat ad infinitum..
```

Note:

Though all of this is on a single monitor, I do run a multi-monitor setup with workspace 10 (and only 10) on the second monitor. I haven't switched to it in the above tests but can't rule out that multi-monitor is somehow a factor in this bug.

body:
A really nice feature of Sway is that you don't have to calculate and config the DPIs on HiDPI screens because it take cares of them for you. I think it would be good if hyprland can have this feature.

I also made a similar [issue](https://github.com/qtile/qtile/issues/3389#issue-1151863809) in Qtile.

title: Key repeat not working for raise/lower volume
body:
I set the bindings of keyboard  keys like so:
```
#### Commands bindings
# Volume
bind=,XF86AudioMute,exec,pamixer -t
bind=,XF86AudioRaiseVolume,exec,pamixer -i 5
bind=,XF86AudioLowerVolume,exec,pamixer -d 5
# Screen brightness
bind=,XF86MonBrightnessUp,exec,light -A 5
bind=,XF86MonBrightnessDown,exec,light -U 5
```
and the key repeat for the audio keys is not working, so i am not able to hold the key down to keep raising/lowering the volume.
However, the brightness keys do work.

I used wev to check how the keys are detected, and this is what i found:
-  In the case of volume keys, and also audio mute, only the release is detected.
- In the case of brightness keys, only the press and repeat is detected, but they are detected as release.
- I also tried `XF86AudioMicMute`, and it detects only the press, but as 2 events: press and release at the same time.

title: toggling fullscreen mode 1 on a floating window on and off will not revert it to its original geometry
body:
### Steps to reproduce 
(start with a tiled window)
```sh
hyprctl dispatch togglefloating ""
hyprctl dispatch resizeactive exact 600 200
hyprctl dispatch centerwindow ""
sleep 1
hyprctl dispatch fullscreen 1
sleep 1
hyprctl dispatch fullscreen 1
hyprctl dispatch moveactive 100 100
```

### Expected outcome
The floating window should be returned to its original size.

### Actual outcome
Window keeps the the fullscreen size but can be moved around.

### Notes
The issue does not occur with `fullscreen 0`.

PS.:
Why do dispatchers *require* at least one argument. Kinda annoying to always put `""` after dispatchers that don't take arguments.

title: focusing a window with dispatcher doesn't bring it to the front when workspace is in fullscreen mode

4. Focus window 2 (window 1 is no longer seen)
5. Go to another workspace
6. `hyprctl dispatch focuswindow address:$a`

Window 1 should be focused

### Notes
Issue occurs with both fullscreen mode 0 and 1.

title: movefocus in a workspace with fullscreen windows only cylces windows in one direction
body:
When opening more than 2 windows in a workspace and toggling fullscreen the `movefocus` dispatcher only cycles windows in one direction.

It would be nice if `movefocus` could also cycle in reverse order based on given direction, i.e.:
- `movefocus l` and `movefocus u` would be equivalent to `cyclenext prev`
- `movefocus r` and `movefocus d` would be equivalent to `cyclenext ""`

(and the same for `swapnext`)

title: Add option to round corners on layers
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Adds the keyword `roundls` (similar to `blurls`) to add rounded corner to a specified layer.

This is useful because it enables us to have rounder corner and blur on notifications, Rofi, and similar tools. Indeed, even though we can make those applications rounded without Hyprland (using CSS generally), if we do so and also use blur, we will see some artefacts in the windows corner:

![2022-12-16T23:42:44,794219812+01:00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/17860659/208201130-996f3616-3ff8-4928-8844-4d0410344b6c.png)

To fix that, I added the option to render with rounded corners in layers.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

There is not much change, and it seems to work perfectly, but this is my first time working on a WM, so you might want to check everything.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

I hope it is. Let me know if anything isn't right.

title: Fix cycleprev bug introduced in 46891b12cf (#1213)
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

This pull request fixes that `cycleprev` always focuses the next window (like `cyclenext`) instead of the previous one.

The reason for this is an incorrect boolean flag for `getNextWindow()` introduced in commit 46891b12cf belonging to #1213.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

Nothing here.

It is ready for merging.

title: Fix focus not changing on (empty) workspace change
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

When using e.g. `focusmonitor` to switch to a monitor without any windows on it, the focus gets stuck on the last window of the previous monitor.

This pull request fixes this bug by explicitly unfocusing the previous window in such a case.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

Nothing here.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

It is ready for merging.

title: Add 'exact' option for 'splitratio'
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

This pull request adds an `exact` option to `splitratio`. It allows to specify an exact value to set the split ratio to instead of a relative one.
This is useful for scripting purposes as well as resetting the split ratio to a known value.

Consider the following example:

```
bind = [...], splitratio, +0.05       # increase the split ratio by 0.05
bind = [...], splitratio, exact 0.6   # set the split ratio to 0.6
```

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

Additionally, I simplified the function `getPlusMinusKeywordResult()` making it also robust against any amount of whitespaces between `exact` and the provided value. I also replaced all tabs by spaces in the same file according to the style guide.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

It is ready for merging.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

  hyprctl keyword decoration:blur_passes 1

title: Dispatcher for alternating between most recent window in the focus history on the current workspace
body:
This issue technically breaks rule about extending Hyprland with scripts, you can close it without reading further *(if you're a monster!)*. ___ I'm surprised Hyprland doesn't offer functionality to essentially Alt-Tab between windows as seen in KDE, Gnome, Awesome, etc. At first it seems that a simple solution would be to alternate between `cyclenext` and `cyclenext, prev`, like so: ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash TOGGLE=/tmp/hypr-alt-tab.toggle if [ ! -e $TOGGLE ]; then touch $TOGGLE hyprctl dispatch cyclenext "" else rm $TOGGLE hyprctl dispatch cyclenext prev fi ``` But it has issues:

1. Changing workspaces has a chance to break the behavior

2. Changing window focus in any other way has a chance to break the behavior

4. Cosmic rays screwing with the if statement just like they with this list index ;o so you know it's a real issue!

___ To make an actual, working version would require a somewhat heavy script: 1. Subscribe to socket, listen for `activewindow>>>`, call `hyprctl activewindow` to grab the address *(not sure why it's not included in the socket message already)* 2. Segregate history based on workspaces, requires parsing `hyprctl clients` 3. Upkeep saved adresses, another parsing of `hyprctl clients` on many socket updates *(window moving, killing, etc.)* to discard old addresses or move them around based on new workspace ___ Why? Because I suck at coding and I want you to do it for me. But seriously... this is a pretty basic feature that would greatly benefit Hyprland users if included :')

title: Changes to windows not rendering in active workspace while connected to external monitor
body:
# Description
Hyprland doesn't properly render changes to windows in the active workspace when launching or killing applications, and when opening GUI dropdown/pop-up menus while connected to an external monitor through HDMI.

Issue goes away if I'm not connected to hdmi.

# Steps to Reproduce
Connected laptop to an external monitor through HDMI. Start hyprland from a tty. Kill or start an application with a hyprland keybind. 

For app menus run anki and within the gui go to Tools > Add-ons. 

Here are my settings
[hyprland.txt](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/files/10312427/hyprland.txt)

# Expected Outcome
When I open or kill a window the workspace will render windows and resize as needed.

title: Scaling in master layout is not rotating with layout
body:
To scale the master window you always drag to the right for bigger and to the left for smaller. This is true even if the master layout have been rotated. 

So if master is on top and slaves at the bottom of screen, you think that expanding master down would be dragging mouse down and dragging mouse up to contract master up. But instead mouse right expands master down, mouse left contract master up. The one slave you can scale are also strange as mouse up contract left and mouse down expands right. 

When master is on right everything feels reversed as dragging mouse right scales master left and dragging mouse right scales master left. But slave scaling feels correct.

Master bottom are also wrong and the problem exists with keybindings too.

Fix so that scaling movement always is the same way that the scaling expands or contract.

title: Master layout slaves are able to scale.
body:
In the wiki: 

> The right, “slave” windows will always be split uniformly. You cannot change their size.

But in reality you can change their size.
This is sometimes helpful as you maybe have three windows and just want to read something from one slave as you work in master. If this scaling behavior should stay all slaves should be scalable. Right now the last slave in the stack is not scalable but all the others are.

title: Add an option to disable wrapping for movefocus
body:
There's a `focus_wrapping` option in sway config.
- The default option is `focus_wrapping=yes`, which behaves the same as Hyprland.
- Set `focus_wrapping=no` will disable move to left when current focused window is already the most left window. Likewise for other directions.

Here's the doc for this option in `man 5 sway`.
> focus_wrapping yes|no|force|workspace
    This option determines what to do when attempting to focus over the edge of a container. If set to no, the
    focused container will retain focus, if there are no other containers in the direction. If set to yes, focus
    will be wrapped to the opposite edge of the container, if there are no other containers in the direction. If
    set to force, focus will be wrapped to the opposite edge of the container, even if there are other containers
    in the direction. If set to workspace, focus will wrap like in the yes case and additionally wrap when moving
    outside of workspaces boundaries. Default is yes.

Hope for a similar config option for Hyprland.

I also found that `movewindow` does not wrap in Hyprland. It would be more consistent to have same behavior for both `movewindow` and `movefocus`

title: Scaling settings for xwayland on hidpi monitor overwritten after a while
body:
So I have a single 4k monitor, following the instruction on the wiki, I installed hyprland with patched xwayland and wlroots and set up the monitor and scaling in my config like this:

`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf`:

```conf
monitor = , 3840x2160@60, 0x0, 2
exec-once =xprop -root -f _XWAYLAND_GLOBAL_OUTPUT_SCALE 32c -set _XWAYLAND_GLOBAL_OUTPUT_SCALE 2
```

hyprland wrapper:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env sh
# vim: ft=sh ts=4 sw=4 sts=4 et :

cd ~

export GDK_SCALE=2
export QT_AUTO_SCREEN_SCALE_FACTOR=1
export QT_QPA_PLATFORM="wayland;xcb"
export QT_QPA_PLATFORMTHEME=qt5ct
export XCURSOR_SIZE=48
export XCURSOR_THEME=breeze_cursors
export XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Hyprland
export XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP=Hyprland
export XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland
export _JAVA_AWT_WM_NONREPARENTING=1

exec Hyprland
```

It works as expected, however after around 30 ~ 60s all xorg apps will spawn with giant UI. I suspect `_XWAYLAND_GLOBAL_OUTPUT_SCALE` is reset to 1 for some unknown reason, because after I run `xprop -root -f _XWAYLAND_GLOBAL_OUTPUT_SCALE 32c -set _XWAYLAND_GLOBAL_OUTPUT_SCALE 2` again the issue is gone temporarily -- after a while the scaling factor is reset again and I have to manually set it to 2 once more.

I'm trying to find some workarounds like executing this command every time a new app is spawned via a hook or something like that, but haven't find a way to achieve that in Hyprland yet.

title: Add "on" and "off" for the bind of switch
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
The old bind for lid switch cannot know whether the lid is open or close.
This PR add "on" and "off" for binding of switch

The old way:
```
bindl=,switch:Lid Switch, exec, switch.sh
```
switch.sh:
```bash
if grep open /proc/acpi/button/lid/LID0/state; then
    hyprctl keyword monitor "eDP-1, 2560x1600, 2560x700, 2"
else
    hyprctl keyword monitor "eDP-1, disable"
fi
```

You can write it now:
```
bindl=,switch:on:Lid Switch, exec, "hyprctl keyword monitor "eDP-1, 2560x1600, 2560x700, 2"
bindl=,switch:off:Lid Switch, exec, hyprctl keyword monitor "eDP-1, disable"
```

title: How do I set resolution for Xwayland applications?
body: I have an external monitor which is set to 2560x1440@144hz. Nothing else. This works as expected for Wayland clients. However, when running something under Xwayland, applications interpret the resolution as 5120x2880. How can I fix this?

title: Implement urgency hint for workspaces
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

There is `focus_on_activate` variable, which unconditionally focuses a window as soon as it requests activation.

This is not always desired, for example if you are working and a chat app requests activation because someone messaged you.

This PR is a first step towards allowing controlled handling of windows that request activation.

With it, every workspace that has an unfocused window that requests activation, will be marked as urgent, following e.g. sway's behavior. If there are multiple windows requesting activation, all of them need to receive focus, before workspace will have its urgency status removed.

Panels like waybar already handle this, and mark the workspace e.g. in a special color. 

In order to test, you need to find an app that can request activation (for example kitty terminal) and a way to see whether workspace is urgent (for example waybar), and then you can test like so:

1. Open workspace 1
1. Open 1st kitty, run `sleep 2 && printf '\a'`
1. Open 2nd kitty
1. Move to workspace 2
1. After 2s, observe that workspace 1 is marked as urgent
1. Move to workspace 1, focus is on 2nd kitty, so workspace is still urgent, as 1st kitty was not focused yet
1. Move focus to the 1st kitty - workspace will no longer be marked as urgent.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I didn't handle XWayland as I am both not sure how to test, and how to mark workspace as urgent. Unless you know how to do it and can give me a hint, maybe this could be added separately, by a more knowledgeable person?

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Yes, unless you want to wait for XWayland implementation before merging.

The next step would be implementing a dispatcher that can focus either the next urgent workspace, or go to the last workspace, thus allowing you with one keybinding to check the chat app and then go back to work. But this will come in a separate PR.

title: Invalid behavior: "Relative workspace on monitor" is actually relative open workspace on monitor
body:
https://wiki.hyprland.org/Configuring/Dispatchers/#workspaces

When switching to the next or previous workspace on a monitor with `hyprctl dispatch workspace m+1` instead of switching to the next workspace hyprland will switch to the next open workspace on the monitor as if the command executed was `hyprctl dispatch workspace me+1` . From what I understand though this command doesn't exist. 
This problem also occurs with `hyprctl dispatch movetoworkspace m+1` so the problem is probably in the implementation of the 'm' parameter.

I think the monitor parameter should do what it says and just switch to the next workspace on the monitor and only if combined with the 'e' parameter should it switch to the next open workspace on the monitor.

TLDR:

Current behaviour:
  `hyprctl dispatch workspace e+1`     --> switch to the next open workspace
  `hyprctl dispatch workspace m+1`    --> switch to the next open workspace on current monitor 
  `hyprctl dispatch workspace me+1`  --> not defined?

Expected behaviour:
  `hyprctl dispatch workspace e+1`    --> switch to the next open workspace
  `hyprctl dispatch workspace m+1`   --> switch to the next workspace on current monitor 
  `hyprctl dispatch workspace me+1` --> switch to the next open workspace on current monitor.

title: remove IsSwitchingToPrevious variable and checks
body:
fixes #1218

#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
it removes the IsSwitchingToPrevious variable from the previous workspace logic. this means that when switching to a previous workspace, switching to the previous workspace again will bring you to the window that switched to previous workspace ie; workspace 1 > previous workspace 2 > previous  workspace 1 > previous  workspace 2

this is in line with it's implementation on other window managers, as well as more consistent with what is expected when switching to the previous workspace.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
could break some workflows, although I can't seem to find anyone that wanted this behavior, apart from maybe the original coder of this functionality. using this alone for a few days, I haven't seen anything break, nor have I seen this variable in other parts of the project.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
maybe it's better to have a config option to decide this rather than a hardcoded fix. I don't think there's any problems with this patch apart from that.

title: Autoreload of configuration doesn't work when configuration path is not default path
body:
Archlinux aur hyprland-git.

Configuration autoreload only works if configuration is located at `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf`

If configuration is provided through Hyprland command, like `Hyprland -c /my/config` and path is not the default path mentioned above then any changes to `/my/config` is not reloaded in Hyprland session.

In addition, if `/my/config` has errors then error message shown in Hyprland session has path written as `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf` instead of `/my/config`

Its possible that Hyprland is reverting to default config path after initial startup even if custom configuration is provided.

title: Fullscreen applications detect as being launched on the first monitor in the chain
body:
Fullscreen applications such as games (tried The Outer Worlds on Steam via Proton, and Cyberpunk 2077 on Heroic via VKD3D) behave as if they are being launched on the first monitor in the virtual layout, "reading" left-to-right.

This happens even if the game is physically being launched in a different monitor. At best this results in the resolution being detected incorrectly and at worst results in an unaddressable window that exists in a limbo-state between being on one monitor and on another.

**Steps to reproduce**
Configure Hyprland such that 
```
monitor=DP-1, 2560x1440@144,1920x0,1
monitor=DP-2, 1920x1080@60,0x0,1
```
and launch a game on DP-1

**Expected outcome**
Game launches on DP-1, fetches the resolution of DP-1 and lets you adjust it to the max of the monitor

**Noted outcome**
Game launches on DP-1, but fetches the resolution of DP-2 but only lets you adjust resolution to the max of DP-2 monitor


I tested a reverse configuration of 
```
monitor=DP-1, 2560x1440@144,0x0,1
monitor=DP-2, 1920x1080@60,2560x0,1
```
,placing DP-2 to the right of DP-1. Doing this, the game detects the resolution correctly, which leads me to believe this is a bug with Hyprland/wlroots or possibly Wine. If this is the wrong place to post, please direct.

title: Unbreak build with libc++

Affects systems where Clang is default e.g., FreeBSD, OpenBSD, OpenMandriva, Chimera Linux. To test on GCC-based systems try:
```
$ export CC=clang CXX=clang++ CXXFLAGS=-stdlib=libc++
$ meson setup /tmp/hyprland_build
$ meson compile -C /tmp/hyprland_build
```

Note, [requires](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/b8cb1dc9ea87) libc++ >= 16 (libc++ 15 can use [`-fexperimental-library`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/deb3b5552f04)) to [avoid](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/0e3dc1a52ffe) the following:

    return std::ranges::all_of(str.begin(), str.end(), [&](char c) { return isdigit(c) != 0 || c == '-' || (allowfloat && c == '.'); });

title: Crash with multiple users on same machine
body:
:wave: Hello!  I am seeing that Hyprland does not like it when there are multiple users on the same machine who use hyperland.  My use case is that I have a machine that I like to use for both work and non-work, so I have 2 separate linux users (`grant` and `grant-work`).  

The issue comes from the fact that Hyprland creates a parent directory in `/tmp`.  So if I run Hyprland as `grant`,  the `/tmp/hypr` folder will be created, owned by `grant`.  If I then switch over to `grant-work` and attempt to run Hyprland, it will crash with a permissions issue, because `grant-work` cannot create a sub-directory in `/tmp/hypr`. 

The main issue stems from line 41 of Main.cpp:

https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/445f8c71c50ed9cdd72299b2ddf696b7baeb1b03/src/main.cpp#L41

I am wondering if we could change the temporary directory to include the username, so that multiple instances of Hyprland could be run on separate TTYs.  

I am happy to create a PR, but I'd love some guidance from the leadership of this project first :slightly_smiling_face:

title: Sometimes Hyprland advertises mirrored external monitor. This makes grim sad.
body:
I have an external monitor and this in my config file:

```
# MONITORS
# See https://wiki.hyprland.org/Configuring/Monitors/
monitor=eDP-1,preferred,auto,1
monitor=HDMI-A-1,preferred,auto,1,mirror,eDP-1
```

Normally Hyprland only advertise the laptop monitor (the mirrored one):
```
interface: 'zxdg_output_manager_v1',                     version:  3, name: 21
	xdg_output_v1
		output: 45
		name: 'eDP-1'
		description: 'AU Optronics 0xAF90 (eDP-1)'
		logical_x: 0, logical_y: 0
		logical_width: 1920, logical_height: 1080
```

But sometimes it decides it is proper to advertise both of them:
```
interface: 'zxdg_output_manager_v1',                     version:  3, name: 21
	xdg_output_v1
		output: 47
		name: 'HDMI-A-1'
		description: 'Samsung Electric Company C24F390 H4LT305839 (HDMI-A-1)'
		logical_x: -1337420, logical_y: -1337420
		logical_width: 1920, logical_height: 1080
	xdg_output_v1
		output: 45
		name: 'eDP-1'
		description: 'AU Optronics 0xAF90 (eDP-1)'
		logical_x: 0, logical_y: 0
		logical_width: 1920, logical_height: 1080
```

Since the external monitor has very low logical position, and since grim tries to capture both of them, grim computes an image size that far exceeds available memory and crashes.

When, in the future, it will not crash, it will error out smoothly without supporting this use case.

See [grim issue 85](https://todo.sr.ht/~emersion/grim/85).

title: Creating a new workspace on monitor if using `m+1`
body:
Hi,

i would like to suggest the feature, that if using a `relative workspace to monitor (m+1)` argument in a `workspace` or `movetoworkspace/movetoworkspacesilent` dispatcher, a new workspace should be created instead of doing nothing in the case of the `workspace` dispatcher.
As an alternative `monitor+next` and `monitor+previous` as a new workspace choice may also be an option, although they imo do not differ that much from `m+1` and `m-1`.

This could be beneficial to users in a multi-monitor setup, as they could just move back and forth between workspaces on a monitor instead of having to assign workspaces to outputs or remember the assigned workspaces.

TL;DR expected behaviour
If a monitor has only one workspace and `hyperctl dispatch workspace m+1` is called, a new empty workspace should be created

title: Option to enable VRR for fullscreen clients
body:
Currently the (seemingly) only option for enabling/disabling VRR is:

```
misc {
    no_vfr = true/false
}
```

It would be cool to expand that a bit with and allow setting it with window rules or similar, but an easy middle-ground option might just be to allow you to enable VRR when a client is fullscreened and disable it when no client is. Similar to how the inhibit rule can be applied to fullscreen clients.

Being able to just set something like `misc:enable_vfr` to `fullscreen` would cover almost all my VRR needs.

title: Trailing whitespace after an argument followed by a comment seems be treated as part of the argument
body:
That is, if trailing comments are at all allowed, of course. They seem to be in binds without argument, though.

`bind = $myMod SHIFT, i, changegroupactive, b # previous tab` -> cycles forward instead of backward (falls back to default?)
`bind = $myMod SHIFT, o, changegroupactive, f # next tab` -> works as expected, but actually also falls back to forward which happens to be correct
`bind = $myMod SHIFT, i, changegroupactive, b ` (no comment, with trailing space) -> cycles backward
`bind = $myMod SHIFT, i, changegroupactive, b` (no comment, no trailing space) -> cycles backward

title: Cursor snaps back to original position after dragging event in certain applications.
body:
### **The Issue**
In certain applications, my cursor resets it's position after dragging on the screen. On further inspection, it appears to only occur in applications where some kind of cursor constraints are applied. 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8363722/217341660-d868c888-a2b0-4694-a8bf-b1fca261d22a.mp4

**Findings**
- At first I thought this was an issue exclusively to blender. It happened after dragging panels and moving objects in the 3d viewport. However, the same issue occurs in VMWare player when clicking and dragging anywhere.
- I know blender constrains the cursor with wayland support ([this](https://projects.blender.org/blender/blender/issues/98714) issue seems very similar). VMware Player also seems like it expects to lock a cursor to the VM.
- Before making this issue, I tried to reproduce the problem with Gnome DE (both Wayland and Xorg) and even another wlroots based compositor (Sway), but to no avail. That's why I believe this issue may be specific to Hyprland.
- With blender, this problem only occurs when running in Wayland mode. (sidenote: this also causes blender to open in a "fake fullscreen mode", where it seems to ignore all windows and just open across the screen. Only after opening the preferences window, blender returns to being regularly tiled). When opening blender with xwayland, this issue does not occur. With VMWare player the issue occurs, even though it's run with xwayland.
- I DO use Hyprland-nvidia-git with an RTX 3080, if that matters. I installed the nvidia-open-dkms on the regular linux kernal for Arch linux 6.1.9-arch1-2. 


---
**Steps to reproduce**
- Install Blender - or possibly another application with cursor constraints(?)
- press mouse button down and move the cursor
- release mouse button

**Expected Outcome**
- Cursor position after release should be the same as the cursor position on release

**Noted Outcome**
- Cursor position returns to the position the cursor was at when the mouse was clicked.

title: Added support for layoutmsg params and added the param 'newfocus' for 'swapwithmaster' and 'focusmaster'
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

It adds the possibility to add parameters to the `layoutmsg` dispatcher for the Master layout.
It also adds the parameter `newfocus` for the `layoutmsg` dispatchers `swapwithmaster` and `focusmaster`,
which can have the following values for `swapwithmaster`:
* `master` - focus at the new master after swap
* `child` - focus the new child after swap
* `auto` - keep the focus on the previously focused window (default and also current behavior)

For `focusmaster` it can have the following values:
* `master` - focus the master, or keep the focus at master if it is already focused
* `auto` - swap the focus with the first child, if the current focus was master, otherwise focus master (default and also current behavior)

Fixes #674 with for example the following binding:
```
bind = $mod,P,layoutmsg,swapwithmaster master
```

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

The PR itself doesn't introduce any breaking compatibility.

I think `CVarList` should have `size() == 0` when the given parameter for the constructor is an empty string (while it is `1` and the first parameter is the empty string).

I haven't changed this behavior in fear that anything breaks that depends on the current behavior.

I'm working around it with a check like this right now: `CVarList::size() > 0 && vars[0] != ""`.


#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Yes it's ready for merge, though we might need to update the hyprland-wiki as well with the new Master layout layoutmsg para, should I add a PR there?

title: Intellij IDEA dialogs "do not show up" in a multi monitor environment
body:
When running a multi monitor setup IntelliJ/Idea dialogs such as file copy & paste, exit confirmation and other dialogs will either not show or flicker between two monitors until the popup window is focused or not "show" at all. 

The issue seems only to be triggered when IntelliJ is running on the secondary monitor. Can't be reproduced in a nested Hyprland session. Does not happen on sway 1.8 stable.

The issue can be only triggered when launching / using Intellij on `DP-1, 3840x2160, 3840x0, 1`.  When running 
on `monitor = DP-2, 3840x2160, 0x0, 1` everything works correctly. 

Multiple effects can be observed ranging from semi functional to non functional / breaking.

Splashscreen flickers between DP-1 (at correct, centered-ish position) and DP-2 (@0x0 / left corner)

title: Valid shell command fails silenty when using the exec dispatch
body:
# The bug

The following shell command would succeed in `sh`
```bash
(command; (test $? == 0) && doSomethingOnError)) | doSomethingWithTheOuput
```
But when set as a dispatch through a keybind, it wont run at all. Which is confusing.
```
bind = , key, exec, (command; (test $? == 0) && doSomethingOnError)) | doSomethingWithTheOuput
```

## Cause
After a little bit of digging, I found that it fails because hyprland is injecting some variables before the command by modifying the command itself, which is leading to a syntax error.
```
[LOG] Executing WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 DISPLAY=:0 (true; (test $? == 0) && notify-send -a title "text")
```

## Workaround
Putting a `;` before the command removes the syntax error, but that's not the best solution and just a frustrating experience overall.
```
bind = , key, exec, ;(command; (test $? == 0) && doSomethingOnError)) | doSomethingWithTheOuput
```

## Fix
If possible, inject the variables without modifying the command itself. Basically, make no assumption about the command.

title: New window management around groups.
body:
At the moment, we do not have the ability to open a tiled window in a workspace filled with a group window.
Maybe we can approach this with a dispatcher to select the workspace (or selecting it with the mouse if gaps are present):
- If the workspace is selected, new windows become tiled. 
- If the group is selected, new windows become grouped.

Luckily you can use `ydotool` that creates a virtual mouse.
But you cannot perform a click on some things, with the touchscreen, e.g. `hyprctl kill` even when a mouse is connected.

title: changegroupactive dispatcher's param no longer works
body: The group/tab rework has changed the `changegroupactive` dispatcher to no longer use its parameter, instead always switching to the next tab. This means there is no way to go to the previous tab anymore.

title: Grouping and ungrouping window causes weird state
body:
If you do these steps:
- open two windows
- group the focused one
- switch focus to the other one, group and ungroup it
- move it into the group with the first window
Then you'll have a group with two windows in it, but the little tab indicator at the top doesn't update when you switch between them, and when you create a window in the group with window 1 focused, it will make it so you can only switch between and access window 1 and that new window.

title: `workspace,previous`  doesn't work with `focuswindow`
body:
Hi,

First of all, thank you for this awesome project.

The issue I'm facing, is when using `focuswindow` to switch and the activated window is in a different workspace, `workspace,previous` binding doesn't work. I think, when using `focuswindow` the active workspace is not getting updated. 
Added a sample config to reproduce.

```conf
# Configuration for window sticking
windowrulev2 = workspace 1,class:^(kitty)$
bind = $mainMod, space, focuswindow, kitty
windowrulev2 = workspace 2,class:^(firefox)$
bind = $mainMod, f, focuswindow, firefox
windowrulev2 = workspace 3,class:^(Slack)$
bind = $mainMod, s, focuswindow, slack

# Move active window to a workspace with mainMod + SHIFT + [0-9]
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 1, movetoworkspace, 1
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 2, movetoworkspace, 2
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 3, movetoworkspace, 3
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 4, movetoworkspace, 4
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 5, movetoworkspace, 5
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 6, movetoworkspace, 6
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 7, movetoworkspace, 7
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 8, movetoworkspace, 8
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 9, movetoworkspace, 9
bind = $mainMod SHIFT, 0, movetoworkspace, 10

# Cycle workspace
bind=ALT,TAB,workspace,previous
```

Steps to reproduce

1. start terminal in 1st workspace
2. start firefox in second workspace
3. press alt-tab # Works fine..
4. press `super+3` to switch to a new workspace
5. press `super+space` to switch to terminal
6. pres alt-tab # Doesn't work

title: Window resolution and cursor size with weird behavior
body:
First of all, thank you very much for this project, I really love Hyprland.

So, for the past few weeks, I've been configuring Hyprland to my personal needs in my Desktop computer (Arch Linux). Everything worked great (even with a NVIDIA GPU!), but, now, I want to use my setup in my notebook as well (also Arch).

However, after installing everything on my notebook, I noticed that the cursor size kept shrinking and expanding depending on which window was active and the windows themselves seemed to have the wrong resolution.

I don't know if I did something stupid in my config, so I tried reinstalling arch linux and, once logged in, I just installed the `hyprland` and the `librewolf-bin` (my browser) packages without any configs or customizations. I just changed the shortcut SUPER + Q to open librewolf instead of kitty and the window had the same behavior as previously. Therefore, I am assuming this issue has nothing to do with my customizations.

## Steps to reproduce
- Install `hyprland` using `yay`
- Install any other program
- Open the installed program in Hyprland

The windows should open normally, without any changes to their resolution

## Noted outcome
I recorded a video showcasing what is exactly happening [here](https://youtu.be/uvcB0vH1-N4). You can see that the window sizes are unusually large (I have a 1920x1080 display) and the weird size of the mouse cursor.

Thanks again for this amazing compositor and I am sorry if I missed something very obvious.

title: Added center orientation to master layout
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

This adds support for a new orientation for master layout.  It is very close to the request in #1250 .

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

For my workflow I prefer my main work window to be centered.  So, this implementation centers the master window immediately when a single slave is created.  This may be a bit awkward for some folks as this leaves empty space on the right side.  If there is a strong preference I can change this to split into halves when only two windows are open.

Only other issue I found is that the mouse resize operation is a bit wonky when in this mode.

The following was added to the master layout config:
 
- orientation: added "center"
- always_center_master: bool - only used for center orientation - if true, while in center orientation the master window will always occupy the center of the screen, otherwise center orientation behaves like left orientation until three windows are open
- layoutmsg: orientationcenter

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

See above.

title: Ensure plugin cleanup on exit
body:
# Why
Simple plugins that just add visuals or hook onto existing code are fine being dropped unexpectedly, since they are self-contained in the process. More advanced plugins, like a plugin manager I'm working on, potentially interact with outside things like the filesystem.

Being able to clean up on unload is necessary, and currently when shutting down Hyprland ignores unloading plugins.

title: Unload plugins on compositor cleanup
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Unloads plugins (in reverse order of loading) on compositor cleanup i.e. exit.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
The current plugins out there don't benefit much from it, and should have clean exits anyway, so it shouldn't break compatibility. As bigger plugins appear I would predict this will be useful enough to warrant being the default, instead of forcing each plugin to hook the exit and do it on its own.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
The functionality is there. Potentially it might be useful to be able to mark plugins as "special" and only unload those, but I'm not sure introducing inconsistency like that will do any good really.

title: When the last display is disconnected, or fails, the entire workspace and applications running inside the session are terminated
body:
I first noticed this when my computer, which is attached to a full-blown television, would suddenly end a remote gameplay session, or I would lose my terminal windows when somebody in the other room turned on the TV to stream video content.

Update: Given the log message I found, it looks like the developers are aware this is an issue?   My apologies if there is, all I found earlier in a search was something about suspend/resume on a laptop not working.

  
## Steps to reproduce:
1.  Disconnect your second display.
2. Launch a terminal window or some applications
3. Simulate a display cable failure, or a pet chewing on your cables, by disconnecting your HDMI adapter.
4. Reconnect it.

## Expected Result:
- Hyprland (and really any WM) should be smart enough to realize that the last display has been removed, and it should try to maintain its workspace in-memory until the system has a viable display again.  

## Observed Result:
- Wallpaper daemon blanks out.
- Applications are all terminated.

title: Floating layout
body:
Similar to dwm's `<><` mode where all windows in a single workspace are set to floating.

Some customizable option ideas to supplement this feature:
- Set new floating windows to open next to each other, like in GNOME
- Set new floating windows to open on top of each other with a slight offset, like with XFCE
- Floating layout available as a default workspace layout
- ~choose for only popups (small windows <= some size) to open in floating mode~ I believe it does this already


Why?
- Programs that create many continuous popups destroy the tiled layout
- Many people manually float each window for a ricing screenshot
- Tiling is not efficient for workspaces with many GUI applications that are not meant to be maximized or squished into a tiny dwindle container
- the current workaround for floating as default (`float,.*; move cursor -50% -50%,.*`) is not very efficient
- new floating windows opening next to each other is better than centering 10+ floating windows on top of each other and having to drag each one away

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/111794344/222600889-1aa3c03c-89d3-439b-acfb-a9ad97be925a.png)

title: Fix clang compilation
body:
void* + integral type is not allowed on standard C++ and is a GNU extension. This PR explicitly casts every void* to uint8_t* when used with pointer arithmetic to fix compilation with clang.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
Since void doesn't have a size in the C++ spec, one cannot perform pointer arithmetic with it. (https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/operator_arithmetic#Additive_operators).
According to GNU spec (https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Pointer-Arith.html) void is considered 1 byte, so pointer arithmetic with void* is allowed for GCC. uint8_t is also 1 byte large, so the calculations are the exact same.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Ready for merging

title: Optionally expose time to screen shaders
body:
This PR adds a way to have access to time in screen shaders. Time is essential for advanced, animated post-process shader effects (i.e. CRT effect, glitch effects, ...). 
Since that requires damage tracking to be disabled, I implemented it as "Pay for what you use". This means time is only added, if it is actually used in the shader; and users that don't use it have no disadvantage. 
If damage tracking is enabled and time is used an error is displayed. 

Implements part of https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/1502

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
This requires, that "damage_tracking = 0" updates every frame, which seems to be the case.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Ready. Criticisms/suggestions welcome though.

title: Buffer over-read in removeBeginEndSpacesTabs()
body:
If a string given to removeBeginEndSpacesTabs() was only tabs/spaces, or had tabs/spaces followed by a comment, it would lead to buffer over-read. 

The reason is that the code `str.length() != 0` , doesn't do anything, since we don't modify the string inside the while loop. Because of this the loop will run forever until `str.length() - countAfter - 1` wraps around and tries to read memory beyond the scope of the string.

title: config: unbreak on BSDs due to undeclared `environ`
body:
According to [POSIX](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/xrat/V4_xbd_chap08.html):
> The variable *environ* is not intended to be declared in any header, but rather to be declared by the user for accessing the array of strings that is the environment. This is the traditional usage of the symbol. Putting it into a header could break some programs that use the symbol for their own purposes.

Neither [DragonFly](https://man.dragonflybsd.org/?command=environ&section=7) nor [FreeBSD](https://man.freebsd.org/environ/7) nor [NetBSD](https://man.netbsd.org/environ.7) nor [OpenBSD](https://man.openbsd.org/man7/environ.7) declare `environ` in any header like POSIX suggested. However, Linux (bionic, glibc, musl) declares `environ` in `<unistd.h>`.

title: Fix plugin argument-less hyprctl calls
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
The current way of internal hyprctl commands adds whitespace at the end of the call. Due to the way `HyprCtl::getReply` handles argument-less commands like "version", the whitespace added by `HyprlandAPI::invokeHyprctlCommand` breaks the hard comparison of eg. `"version" == "version "`. This fixes that by just not adding unnecessary whitespace.

title: Workspace switch on mouse exiting screen edge (mouse exiting screen events?)
body:
I would find it very useful if the workspaces could be switched by mouse gestures in the following manner:

When the mouse reaches the right side of the screen and moves a little bit more the active workspace should switch to the next one. On the left side it should switch to the previous in the same manner.

I would like to suggest two possible ways to implement this:

1. Have it as a separate setting in Hyprland. An option to set the desired move distance should exist in order to set the distance that the mouse should move to play the switch animation and actually switch. If the gesture is interrupted before the mouse travels this distance outside the screen the switch should be cancelled. 

2. Implement a way to be able to bind actions to the mouse exiting the screen at the left, right, top and bottom of the screen from the config (perhaps have a global threshold of the traveled distance necessary for the dispatch or have 4 global settings for each one separately or just the top-bottom and right-left pairs, depending on how granular you want this feature to be). This would be more flexible for the general use case, and could, perhaps be the better way to go. This could be used in conjunction with these events to implement the feature I desire and give users more flexibility at the same time.
This could look something like:
```
bind=mouse_left_exit,workspace,-1
bind=mouse_right_exit,workspace,+1
```
The names could be refined to `mouse_left_exit_screen` or something more reasonable, but I think you get the idea.
This second idea could also allow these gestures to combine with modifier keys, allowing for even more flexibility.

title: Support for sway/i3 style modes
body:
In sway/i3 you can create a menu that partially overylays the bar with something like the below. The benefits are that you can create a modal submenu of sorts, and you can get a visual of the mode key mappings.

I looked through the docs and didn't see anything that could provide this, if I missed it please point me to the section or function.

sway example:
~~~
bindsym $mod+Shift+z mode "(l)ock, (e)xit, (f)reeze, (s)uspend, (h)ibernate, (r)eboot, (p)oweroff"

mode "(l)ock, (e)xit, (f)reeze, (s)uspend, (h)ibernate, (r)eboot, (p)oweroff" {
  bindsym l exec swaylock -l -F -i $wallpaper --scaling fill, mode "default"
  bindsym e exec swaymsg exit
  bindsym f exec doas zzz -s, mode "default"
  bindsym s exec doas zzz -z, mode "default"
  bindsym h exec doas zzz -Z, mode "default"
  bindsym r exec doas reboot
  bindsym p exec doas poweroff
  bindsym Return mode "default"
  bindsym Escape mode "default"
}
~~~

body:

Config:

master {
    new_is_master=false

### Example 1
Create 3 windows labelled as follows:

|---|---|
|   | 3  |

Now select window 3 and add to master, resulting in:
| 1  | 2  |
|---|---|
|  3 |   |

Now, when using the `cyclenext`/`cycleprev` layoutmsg dispatchers, we should see cycling in 1 -> 3 -> 2 order. Hower we don't, we see 1 -> 2 -> 3.

### Example 2
This becomes more obvious in the example above when we add 2 to master instead of 3. We now have arrangement:
| 1  | 3 |
|---|---|
|  2 |   |

We should see  1 -> 2 -> 3. However, we see this breaking down into 2 separate cycles: 1 -> 2 and 2 -> 3, depending on whether we cycle previous or next.

title: Refactor CMake and Make file
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

- modernize CMake a bit
- "unscreamify" CMake commands
- add `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS` to `file(GLOB_RECURSE ...)`, such the CMake configure phase is invoked when new files are added (important for incremental builds)
- replace undocumented CMake option `-H` by `-S` in Makefile
- remove unnecessary "cd" in Makefile
- call `meson setup <build-dir>`, because `meson <build-dir>` is deprecated

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

Let me know if that went too far for the first round of refactoring.

Ready to merge.

i found this issue on the llvm project

g function for call to '__begin'
        = decltype(ranges::__cust_access::__begin(std::declval<_Tp&>()));

title: mouse should follow window focus when swapping
body:
Currently when *cycling* through windows the mouse pointer location follows window focus and moves to the center of the newly focused window. 

However when two windows are *swapped* the cursor doesnt move to the new location. This doesn't seem like the most natural behaviour - now when the mouse is next moved it refocuses on the one it was swapped with.

I think it would make the most sense to have the mouse always follow window focus during these operations - unless I am missing something?

title: Keycodes are overloaded by key names for single numbers
body:
I think you have a bug in bind: it recognize both the keycodes mentionned in wev (ex: 64 for Alt_L) and the keynames (Alt_L)

However, the single digit keycodes 1..9 are taken over by the number keys of the same name, this is visible if you want to specify a bind to the actual Escape keycode (9):

     bindr=,9,exec, foot

It gets executed instead executed when you press 9.

A solution would be either a toggle (to avoid having to change config files), or requiring the use of the full names for number keys, so "Nine" not 9 which should unambiguously mean the keycode.

     # Esc (keycode 9) opens a terminal
     bindr=,9,exec, foot
     # The number nine does whatever
     #bindr=,Nine,...

This will be mostly seen with a modifier as the number keys are often accessed directly, but some minimalist keyboard layouts omit the number keys so it could be a problem for them.

Even outside of this specific case, i's not always possible to just use the keynames: for examples, if using the kb_options you can have 2 different keycodes both sending the same keyname (ex: caps:ctrl_modifier: both the caps and lctrl key will send Control_L) which necessitates the use of keycodes in bindr mappings to disambiguate

title: Add config to disable xdp warnings
body:
Since hyprland sets `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Hyprland` and imports it into the dbus activation environment, `xdg-desktop-portal` tries all implementations in the following order:

1. All portals with `UseIn=Hyprland`, in lexicographical order by the filenames under `/usr/share/xdg-desktop-portal/portals/`
2. All portals without `UseIn=Hyprland`, also in lexicographical order by filenames.

In cases like screenshot and screencast, it will stop when it finds the first portal that claims to have the interface in the `Interface=` key.

So even if both `hyprland.portal` and `wlr.portal` are installed, the portal will use `hyprland.portal` for screenshot and screencast since they both have the `UseIn=Hyprland` key and `hyprland.portal < wlr.portal`. As for the `kde` and `gnome` portals, they don't have `UseIn=Hyprland` so they will just be fallbacks.

All in all I don't see how having these portal installed will cause issues.

title: Added overflow check for blur radius
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Added a (temporary) fix to prevent blur radius from overflowing. When the value if decoration::blur_size and/or decoration::blur_passes is large, the expression `*BLUR_SIZE * pow(2, *BLURPASSES)` might return a value that won't fit into an `int` so an overflow occurs when the returned value is implicitly casted to an `int` when it gets passed to `wlr_region_expand`.

`wlr_region_expand` has this assertion which made me find out about the overflow:

    assert(distance >= 0);
#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
This is not supposed to be a permanent (or even temporary) fix, I'm sure someone who has a better understanding might figure out something better as I'm not yet familiar with the codebase at all.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Ready for merging.

title: Monitors connected through a Thunderbolt dock are only activated the first time they’re connected
body:
I have three monitors connected to a Thunderbolt dock.
When I connect the dock to my laptop while Hyprland is running _or_ have them connected while booting, they are working as expected.
But if I unplug the Thunderbolt cable, wait for a few seconds, and plug it in again, the monitors don’t receive any signal, even though they show up in the output of `hyprctl monitors`.

- The internal laptop screen is not affected and keeps its name `eDP-1`.
- I noticed that their names (e.g. `DP-1`) aren’t reused but are incremented by 3 (`DP-1` → `DP-4`).
- Surprisingly, restarting Hyprland didn’t help. Only after a full reboot they worked again.
- I also tested this in Gnome (40?) where I didn’t have this problem.

title: [Question] TTY inaccessible from Hyprland?
body:
# Issue
I'm able to switch between different `TTY(num)` sessions when I'm in `TTY0` with `WIN+ALT+F(num)`, e.g: `TTY(1,2,3,x,..)`.

However, as soon as I enter Hyprland this is no longer possible. I'm guessing this is because `mainMod` key is set to WIN button (SUPER).

# Why
This is troublesome since if Hyprland hard-locks/freezes, key bindings stop working like CTRL+M (exit) and you're stuck in a black screen. This can happen when you receive a notification in Brave browser without a notification daemon or sometimes if you try to launch Hyprland with 10bit colors with a Nvidia card.

# Question
How can you access different TTY sessions when inside Hyprland? E.g could it be possible with key binds?

title: wsbind rules deactivate when dpms off is used in a multi monitor configuration
body:
> steps to reproduce

1. Assign different workspaces to each monitor. Say 1-5 to first monitor, 6-10 to second monitor.
2. Simply use any standard idle command through swayidle, like what I use: `swayidle -w timeout 300 'swaylock -f -c 000000' timeout 600 'hyprctl dispatch dpms off' resume 'hyprctl dispatch dpms on' before-sleep 'swaylock -f -c 000000'`
3. Let the dpms switch off the monitors.
4. Move mouse/click on keyboard to wake up monitors.

> Expected outcome

All the open windows and applications to retain their position in each respective workspace and monitor.

> Noted outcome

All aforementioned open windows and applications shift to second monitor, with every workspace -including the ones assigned to first monitor- shifting to the second monitor when they are not supposed to.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

So, basically every time monitors go to sleep. I wake them up, and I have to free up workspace 1-5, then reopen them on the first monitor again, and relaunching/moving around a lot of stuff back. The entire process takes way too long, and should not happen in the first place.

It seems like Hyprland sends all workspaces to the active monitor in case the other is disconnected. Sway does not do that. Which is why it has never been a problem there. Sway will permanently sticky the assigned workspaces to each respective monitor, even in the case of one being disconnected.

title: Running in nested mode overwrites systemd environment variables
body:
When running Hyprland nested for dev/debug it sets systemd  env variables DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY to the nested values, which means any future systemd launched programs have the wrong environment and likely won't work.

Maybe just don't do the systemctl import-environment if running nested? Or allow it to be disabled in the config, since you shouldn't really be running nested without a separate config anyways

title: Update InputManager.cpp
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
fixes #1711 by adding a check for dragging when changing focus from moveMouseUnified in InputManager.cpp. This means that whenever a user drags a window, they cannot change focus with their mouse, and the focus stays on its current window unless changed via keybind.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
Tested a few times before and after the patch. I was unable to change focus as described in #1711 with my patch, whereas without the patch I could reproduce the issue. slightly deeper testing seems to only produce expected behaviors.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
I think this patch is ready for merging.

title: Environment variables in bind exec parsed incorrectly
body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Put `export TERMINAL=kitty` in `.zshenv`.
2. Add `bind = $mod, return, exec, $TERMINAL` to the hyprland config.

### Expected outcome
Kitty or the program set in $TERMINAL is launched.

### Noted outcome
The program is not launched and the following log is created:

> [LOG] Executing WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 DISPLAY=:0 linuxINAL

It seems like $TERM is resolved to "linux" instead of resolving the entire environment variable.

### Workaround
Using `${TERMINAL}` in the bind fixes the issue.

I don't know if this is a bug or not but I found this behavior a bit strange, so I hope that I can at least help anybody who might have come across this.

title: Fix nix build options
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Some of the build options in the Nix derivative currently don't work. For example, setting `legacyRenderer` to `true` does nothing (it is built with the legacy renderer off), and setting `withSystemd` to `false` does nothing (it is built with systemd enabled). I spent a long time debugging why Hyprland was not running with on Asahi Linux even with the legacy renderer on before I realized that the binary was not being built with legacy renderer.

I am not familiar with Meson and am not sure whether this is the right way to implement this. Please let me know if changes need to be made.

title: Version scheme incorrectly using "beta"
body:
Please drop the `beta` suffix from future tagging. The use of the "beta" label in the tag here is not denoting the status of a *specific version*, it is being used to denote the overall status of the *project*. This is evidenced by the fact that the next version after `v0.22.0beta` or similar is never `v0.22.0`, but always another bump like `v0.23.0beta`. In other words these are not beta cuts of a specific tag that isn't marked yet, they **are** the release of that tag—with "beta" tacked on the end so people don't take the project too seriously.

Following either 0ver or semver specs as you prefer is fine, but the current scheme is weird and obnoxious for packagers. The leading zero already suggests the project is in a development mode where breaking changes can happen in any/all releases. Given the volume of uptake already in the wild the "don't use this as your daily driver" ship has sailed.

title: Missing a modifier: META is not a valid mod, and can't be replaced by Mod1 +Mod4 either
body:
If the keyboard has a Meta key, it's a valid modifier.

If the keyboard doesn't have a meta key but if mapping one, for example with `kb_options = ... ctrl:lctrl_meta`,  the left control key is then mapped to Meta_L, which becomes a valid modifier: we can see in wev that Meta_L sets both Mod1 and Mod4

However, META is not a valid modifier for hyprland: adding the following to hyprland.conf causes an error:

    bindr=META,Meta_L,exec, ...

Binding actions to Meta + key don't work either, for ex Meta+a :

    bind=MOD1 MOD4,a,exec, ...

Suggestion: adding META as a valid modifier to allow shortcut using the Meta modifier, eventually adding Mod1 and Mod4 as valid aliases

title: Fix swiping onto a new workspace with multiple monitors.
body:
The previous code could run into issues into the following circumstances:

* The focused monitor is on its rightmost workspace with ID `i`.
* Another monitor has a workspace with ID `i+1`.
* `workspace_swipe_create_new` is enabled.

Then, swiping rightwards attempts to target a new workspace with ID `i+1`: completing the swipe gesture unintentionally focuses that workspace on whichever monitor it's already on while leaving the active monitor in a broken state where it shows no windows but creates new windows on the workspace it was previously on; and cancelling the swipe gesture shifts the entire workspace `i+1` to the right by the width of the active monitor.

By choosing an ID that doesn't exist, this problematic behavior is avoided.  More specifically, it's the smallest ID greater than any existing workspace's ID, because otherwise the new workspace that was seemingly just created to the right of the rightmost workspace could end up somewhere in the middle of the workspace order.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

No issues I'm aware of.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Ready for merging as far as I'm concerned.

title: Move to empty workspace on next monitor with `movefocus` and `movewindow`
body:
I've just moved to hyprland from sway, and I've realized that my workflow pretty much only consists of moving focus/windows in directions. In sway, it was possible to move to an empty workspace with a direction move, and I could also move a window to the next (empty) monitor by moving it in that direction.

In hyprland, it seems like moving the focus to an empty workspace with a direction is not possible at all, and moving a window is only possible if another window is on that workspace already - and the windows will be swapped instead of actually moving the window to the workspace, next to the window already there.

I'm interested in working on this feature myself. Is this feature something you would be open to?
