title: `hyprland#nixosModule` incompatible with `nixos-unstable`
body:
The nixos module added in https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/221730 creates conflicting options with the `nixosModules.default` module.

```console
error: The option `programs.hyprland.enable' in `/nix/store/qyyw6dd6lqlhz3cqap31d071cbyh34bf-source/nixos/modules/programs/hyprland.nix' is already declared in `/nix/store/qyyw6dd6lqlhz3cqap31d071cbyh34bf-source/flake.nix'.
```

I've been able to restore equivalent functionality by just applying the overlay of the hyprland flake instead of the nixos module.

```nix
{
  nixpkgs.overlays = [ inputs.hyprland.overlays.default ];
}
```

Ping @fufexan

title: Allow exceptions to window swallowing
body: As far as I can see, under the current implementation window swallowing is pretty much all or nothing - if I add the terminal in the regex, it will swallow any window it spawns. While that's the desired behaviour almost all the time there's occasionally some exceptions (like `wev`) where you want to keep the default behaviour. Could we add something like `swallow_exception_regex` for this use case?

title: nofocus layerrule
body:
**precondition**

- hyprland v > 0.23
- any bars with layershell (i.e. [eww](https://github.com/elkowar/eww))
- have `:focusable false` in eww yuck config

**str**

1. open any window
2. click on bar

**exp**

- focus kept on window

**act**

- bar gets focus

[df54ab4](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/commit/df54ab40ceb6e7f74844e83d3f55739accd349cc) "allows" focus, but what if it is not desired by default. It's probably achievable with some dispatchers called on i.e. workspaces buttons clicks, but the whole bar has some other stuff :-P
Though having something like `layerrule = nofocus,<namespace>`  would be great
Disabling this internally in eww doesn't work

title: misc:vfr not working in v0.24
body:
**precondition**

- hyprland v > 0.23

- `hyprctl keyword debug:overlay 1`

- fps ~60

title: Allow movefocus for empty workspaces
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

As discussed in #1999, this PR implements moving to and from empty workspaces using `movefocus`.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I've tried to adapt to your naming schemes, but I'm not sure in which cases you use the `P` prefix for variables, and if I'm correct in assuming that all local window/workspace/monitor variables in functions should be all uppercase (e.g. `PNEWWINDOW`). I'd like having at least underscore to separate words for readability (`P_NEW_WINDOW`), but I'll use the current style if that's what you prefer.

I was also wondering, if a workspace has no current focused window, is it possible that there are still windows? I imagine that could happen if a silent move to a workspace occurred. See my TODO in the code for that.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

I was unsure about how this functionality should be activated, since it's potentially breaking the workflow of current users who depend on a fallback to any window if no window is found in the direction. It would also be possible to still do that fallback behavior if no monitor was found in that direction.

My idea would be to add an option to enable the fallback behavior (`getNextWindowOnWorkspace`) and enable it by default.

title: Add ability to split master when only 1 additional window
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Regarding  [Issue: #1836 ](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/1836)
Add functionality to master & stack layout.
this pull request allows the user to optionally enable DWM like master splitting with as few windows as they would like.
````
master {
    allow_small_split = true
}
````

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
Found 3 minor issues:

1. (pre-existing behaviour) when increasing the number of masters on "center" orientation, it is possible to end up with a blank pane to the right  if you add too many masters.
2. (bug with this PR) if you close a window while all windows are masters. they will not re-flow & fill the whole screen until you open a new window.
3. (bug with this PR) if you close the top master window, you cannot select the bottom one until you open a new window.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
It could be merged as an "in development" feature?
otherwise, happy to work on the bugs listed above.

title: swallow: Add swallow_exception_regex
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Currently, if a window class is specified in the swallow_regex (e.g. Kitty) it will swallow every other window spawned by it automatically. Many other WMs implementing this functionality allow for defining exceptions from this rule. For instance, we want Kitty to swallow sxiv or zathura but we do not want Kitty to swallow something like wev.

This commit adds an additional regex - swallow_exception_regex where these exceptions can be defined. This regex is then compared against the title of the window about to be swallowed and if it happens to be a match, aborts the swallowing.

This works because whenever an application that could be swallowed is launched by a terminal, the class of the terminal remains the same while the title changes to whatever the application's name is, thus letting it be matched against a regex.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

The PR should be ready to be merged unless the config option name should be changed for some reason. Presumably the documentation will need to be updated as well.

Solves issue #2002

title: Fix possible usage of clamp with lo > hi in Vector2D (crash)
body:
Vector2D introduced a clamp function as Hyprland would crash if the windows got too small (see #100).
While the implementation might work for some, the usage might result in undefined behavior, as `std::clamp` does not define calling it with `lo > hi`. This is however not checked and will occur if windows get too small.

In my case this results again in a crash due to a failed assertion checking for `lo > hi` in the std library on my system (archlinux).

I am not sure if INFINITY is necessarily the correct value to set here (I just oriented myself to how it was previously), because I am very much missing context (I just wanted to debug this crash real quick).
This patch does however result in Hyprland not crashing no matter how many windows I open (which I think should be the default, lol).
(maybe not infinitely many, but enough that there are lots that are so tiny that they have a size of 0x0)

As the question of "Why in the world would you even create windows that small tho?" remained unanswered in #100, I want to answer it for my case here:
1. have 20px gaps
2. use dwindle layout with preserve_split set to yes and force_split to 2 (resulting in half the window size on each new window)
3. `evince docs{1..15}.pdf`


I would suggest to add an option to automatically open windows in floating mode if the window size of the new window would be below a certain threshold, but an implementation of that would be outside the scope of this PR.

title: Enumerating inactive devices causes performance issues
body:
`Steps to reproduce`
- Install nvidia packages and drivers and tools (i.e. CUDA)
- `Hyprland`

`Expected outcome`
Same performance and responsiveness as without `nvidia` drivers and modules loaded.

`Noted outcome`
Delayed response times from keypress -> action (i.e. spawning terminal)

To clarify, this is not about support for NVIDIA - I only use it for compute-related tasks - I _do_ load `nvidia`, `nvidia-drm`, `nvidia-modeset`, ..., but I explicitly do not enable `nvidia-drm.modeset=1`. On startup, Hyprland (or some dependency) appears to enumerate the NVIDIA GPU but as expected it won't receive any response - however, it keeps attempting to either enumerate or access the device (no logs to confirm this but I believe that's what happening) causing problems in the responsiveness.

Setup TLDR:
- Headless NVIDIA setup for compute
- Integrated Display solely driven by Intel

title: [Regression] `workspace previous` dispatcher breaks if `allow_workspace_cycles` is set to false.
body:
Steps to reproduce
Be on commit 287e6c4ede30c8e5e85863cd85f157e17e24879c or later
set `allow_workspace_cycles = 0`
go to workspaces 1 > 2 > 3
workspace previous

Expected
1 2 [3] > `workspace previous` > 1 [2] 3 > `workspace previous` > [1] 2 3

Noted
1 2 [3] > `workspace previous` > 1 2 [3] (and in the logs: [LOG] No previous workspace to change to)

Other behavior changes noted

- Since I use workspace cycles as a sort of alt-tab between two workspaces, this commit seems to invert the behavior of allow_workspace_cycles. Previously if it was set to false, and you were on workspace 1 > 2 > 3, then workspace previous, they would cycle between 3 and 2, and if set to true, would go 3 > 2 >1, which makes less sense, so the new logic seems to work as intended.

- With `allow_workspace_cycles=1`
Switching from an empty workspace to an active one only works once. Example:
[1] 2 > `workspace 3` > 1 2 [3] > `workspace previous` > [1] 2 > `workspace previous` > 1 2 [3] > `workspace previous` > `[LOG] No previous workspace to change to`. Unsure of what's the intended behavior.

title: blur_xray does not xray with windows on special workspaces
body:
Please consult the issue guidelines at
https://github.com/vaxerski/Hyprland/blob/main/docs/ISSUE_GUIDELINES.md
BEFORE submitting.

Steps to reproduce:

- Turn on blur_xray in hyprland config (with prereqs)
- Open terminal with transparency (in my case foot)
- Float terminal, and see blurred background as expected
- Unfloat terminal, and open terminal on special workspace (scratchpad)
- See blurred everything open, and not background

Expected outcome:

I expected that blur_xray would work the same for floating windows on special workspaces the same as on the same workspace

Noted outcome:

Rather, floating transparent windows on special workspaces will blur all of the opened apps (as pictured) and not the background.

Noticed on Arch 0.24.1-1 package, but I also tested on the latest Hyprland commit, as requested in the above guidelines, and got the same result.

title: [Feature] Preview workspaces
body:
# Issue
Currently when working with multiple workspaces you have to remember where each window is and in which order workspaces are sorted to efficiently navigate between workspaces.

# Solution?
Windows 10+ offers a workspace preview which makes it easy to determinate location of certain windows and switch between workspaces interactively:
![virtualworkspaces-57fe7e193df78cbc2860500d](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45666572/232290205-50308fe3-7153-4c76-81e0-f4bebc40ebb0.png)
This preview also shows workspace names which is already a feature that is supported in Hyprland and it would nicely tie in with a workspace preview overlay/screen.

title: Windows from workspace getting invisible when workspace is moved to different monitor while unfocused
body:
This isn't a breaking issue.

Tested with two monitors.

To reproduce:
- first set two workspaces on monitor A (e.g. 1 and 2);
- set workspace 3 on monitor B;
- move the _unfocused_ workspace of monitor A to monitor B (e.g. while on workspace 1 of DP-1 do: `hyprctl dispatch moveworkspacetomonitor '2 DP-2'`)
- focus monitor B and dispatch to workspace 2

With this all windows from workspace 2 get invisible. A way to get them back is to: open a new window, toggle fullscreen then toggle back, this brings the windows back.

_Originally posted in https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/2077#issuecomment-1510496796_

title: Relative monitor movement behaves counter-intuitive
body:
Relative monitor movements (m+1, m-1) do not take monitor position configurations into account.

I have 3 monitors, in the configuration below:

```
------------   ------------    ------------ 
|           |  |           |   |           |
|     1     |  |     3     |   |     2     | 
|           |  |           |   |           |
------------   ------------    -------------
```

Moving a workspace from monitor 1 with `movecurrentworkspacetomontor ,+1` I would expect it to go to
monitor 3, but goes to monitor 2 instead.

When adjusting this, this might break a lot of configs. Perhaps add a script option (in hyprctl) to get the adjacent monitors
so I can script this.

Not sure if this actually inconsistent (names work the same), but still.

title: ext_workspace_unstable: zext_workspace_handle_v1.activate() is ignored
body:
Relevant issue: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/381

From that issue:
> The protocol itself does not support that

But I think it does? From the protocol:

> ```xml
> <request name="activate">
> 	<description summary="activate the workspace">
> 		Request that this workspace be activated.
> 
> 		There is no guarantee the workspace will be actually activated, and
> 		behaviour may be compositor-dependent. For example, activating a
> 		workspace may or may not deactivate all other workspaces in the same
> 		group.
> 	</description>
> </request>
> ```

title: How to get a "scratchpad" ? A floating terminal toggle by the same keybind.
body:
I want to have a floating terminal every time I keystroke SUPER+grave:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39454079/232846643-fac7edc3-b5f0-4fc4-911e-42813ecf615e.png)

So I bind this:

```
bind = $mainMod, grave , exec , [ float  ; size 60% 50% ] kitty
```

But this bind has a problem that I cannot close it with the same key bind, which I have been used to (from [dwm](https://dwm.suckless.org/patches/scratchpad/)). Even if I bind another key to close it like :

```
bind = $mainMod_SHIFT, grave , killactive,
```

It is quite possible to close other working windows, incorrectly. Is there any way in Hyprland for this need?

By the way, whenever I open a new window, it will break my full screen mode ( 'monocle' layout)  back into master layout. It is really annoying, is there any solution for that?

title: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not set error while installing Hyprland
body:
I was trying to install Hyprland on Manjaro and faced some roadblocks! I have a Nvidia GTX 1060, so when I installed nvidia-dkms driver and rebooted it got stuck at ```dev/sda1: clean, 552599/6111232 files, 7119295/24414464 blocks```, so then I uninstalled the dkms drivers and then reinstalled my linux61-nvidia drivers and now my pc was able to boot.

Next I ran Hyprland command and i got the following error:
```
00:00:00.000 [ERROR] [libseat] [libseat/backend/seatd.c:66] Could not connect to socket /run/seatd.sock: Permission denied
00:00:00.000 [INFO] [libseat] [libseat/libseat.c:76] Backend 'seatd' failed to open seat, skipping

i was getting this error even though **seatd** was installed and running. Then I figured out that seatd can only be ran as sudo (idk why this is happening) but running ```sudo Hyprland``` fixed the previous issue but now I get this error:

aborted
```
I searched alot but couldn't find any solution for this. Please HELP!

title: Resizing with mouse unintuitive if you grab the 'wrong' side of the window
body:
Hello, I was wondering if this is feasible - currently, resizing a tiled window is really unintuitive in comparison to a floating window, as pointed out by PR #1347 .

When floating, the position of the cursor vs the container matters - if you click on the right half of the window it'll grow the window if you drag right, and shrink if you go left. If you grab the left half, it does the opposite.

When tiles however, you can grab the 'wrong' side of a window and the resize mechanism is the opposite. It also makes it hard to change the 'splits', since it means you have to figure out which window controls said split.

If you enable `resize_on_border` the issue is worsened - depending on which part of the gap you drag, you will either get the right or wrong functionality. I'd expect dragging the gap to always allow you to move the split, rather than disturbing some other split. This is just me considering horizontal splits, but as soon as you include vertical the problem gets worse as it could be the correct window for one and not the other.

I believe this is the case in `sway` and even though I hate to do direct comparisons, I do think it would make this a little nicer to daily drive.

Thank you for your hard work :slightly_smiling_face: 

---

### Summary

* Please make it so that the mouse's position is taken into account when resizing a tiled window such that you are stretching the window with the mouse:
  * Dragging right on the right side of the window will grow, and left would shrink.
  * This will mimic the way it's done for floating windows
* Visualised another way, it should look like you're manipulating the splits between windows:
  * Find the closest window corner to where the cursor clicks and change the position of the splits such that the window's corner follows the mouse

Thanks!

title: Window resizing for pseudotiled windows
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Adds resize support to pseudotiled windows. When resizing outside of the window the pseudotiled space is resized, but when resizing inside of the window, the window itself is resized. If the pseudotiled window has a floating size bigger than its pseudotiled area then its floating size is set to the visible pseudotiled size.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
Not sure if you use nested structs at all, haven't seen any in hyprland so far. I used one here.

A lot of code is duplicated from `applyNodeDataToWindow`, this could probably be done better.

Also unsure if theres a better way to get the drag start position for a window.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Yes if the above is not a concern.

# Description
When switching to another workspace with `hyprctl` and the dispatches `moveworkspacetomonitor` and `workspace` on my focused monitor sometimes the workspace on the non-focused monitor also changes.

I'm using a wrapper script to change my workspaces as i prefer to have the new workspace open on my currently active monitor (the Script is "heavily inspired" by https://github.com/taylor85345/hyprland-dotfiles/blob/master/hypr/scripts/workspace which i found through:    https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/747 )

I'm quite new to hyprland and wayland in general, so if i should test anything or provide more logs i would be more than happy to.

# Steps to reproduce
Create the wrapper script and configure the keybinding:
## config: included logging the output for debug purposes
```
[...]
# Switch workspaces with mainMod + [0-9]
bind = $mainMod, 1, exec, bash -c "/home/myusername/scripts/hyprland_show_workspace_clean.sh 1 >> /home/myusername/monitor.log 2>&1"

#! /bin/bash
monitors=$(hyprctl monitors | tr '\n' '\a')

else

  workspace="$1"

echo "current layout:"
hyprctl monitors

if [[ $workspace -eq $passivews ]] && [[ $activemonitor != "$passivemonitor" ]]; then
  echo "workspace: $workspace equals passive monitor workspace: $passivews"
  echo "switching to workspace: $workspace"
  hyprctl dispatch workspace "$workspace"
else
  hyprctl dispatch moveworkspacetomonitor "$workspace" "$activemonitor"
  hyprctl dispatch workspace "$workspace"
  echo "moved workspace: $workspace to monitor: $activemonitor"

fi

echo "current layout:"
hyprctl monitors

## DESCRIPTION

This works
```sh
hyprctl setcursor $cursor_theme $cursor_size
foot
```

This doesn't → setcursor settings will be ignored.

```sh
hyprctl setcursor $cursor_theme $cursor_size
foot --server
footclient
```

## HOW TO REPRODUCE

```sh
# Make it fail
yay -S foot
foot --server
footclient

# Make it work
foot

title: Declarative plugin management
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Allows declaring `plugin` entries in the hyprland configuration.
Plugins will be loaded if an entry is added and unloaded if that entry is removed.

Example:
Loading hyprland with
```
plugin = /absolute/path1.so
```
will load the plugin at that path. Removing the entry from the configuration will unload the plugin.
Adding an entry while hyprland is running will cause it to load the plugin.

This is useful for having a nicer config, and decoratively loading plugins.

Nixos example:

You update your system and your hyprland plugin rebuilds. It now has a different path due to the hash of the plugin's sources. After your update your configuration now looks like this

```diff
 # ...
-plugin = /nix/store/jy7lsy0xzyxpkyydk6biql6gpcsg3xh9-hy3-0.1/lib/libhy3.so
+plugin = /nix/store/38a2886e42a9bc982006f6607a983xh9-hy3-0.1/lib/libhy3.so
 # ...
```

Hyprland notices the change and first unloads the old plugin version. then loads the new one.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
No

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Yes, I'll write the wiki pr shortly.

title: Fix recursion in package overlays
body:
@fufexan 

**Edit:**

It started with the first commit but I've pushed more work and the PR needs some explanation.

# Description

Previously, the way the flake constructed its `packages` output was to call the `overlays.default` output with `null` for the fixed-point and `prev` for the instance of `pkgs` to modify. Instead of using packages from `final` to use in the derivations overridden from `prev`, it would use the `rec` keyword to use packages adjacent.

Now, `packages` is constructed with a new instance of `pkgs` for both `final` and `prev`, and the overlays themselves use `final` and `prev` correctly. This was done so that some flake packages could depend on other packages also exported by the flake. However, because `packages` was created through the use of `overlays`, this is incorrect and defies the purpose of the overlay mechanism.

This new instance of `pkgs` that overlays receive will include all other dependency packages exposed by the flake (and its inputs, in the case of `hyprland-protocols`). This means that anywhere a package was previously used to create an overridden derivation, where it was before using `rec`, it now properly uses the package from `final` recursively, properly utilizing fixed-point extension.

# Why?

The dependency graph was incorrect, and overlay packages instantiated incorrectly.

This fixes the behavior of both overlays and usage of packages, as well as usage of a combination of the two. Previously, Hyprland could not be built if the flake's `default` overlay was applied to current `nixpkgs/nixos-unstable`, because of a version conflict with `wayland-server` (needed `1.22`, has `1.21`). Now the `wayland-latest` overlay will be applied to packages from the `packages` output, and additionally the other overlays from the flake can be used separately without rebuilding everything in *nixpkgs* that depends on `wayland`.

# Is it ready to merge?

Yes

The `overlays.default` output of this repo doesn't use the flake's own `hyprland-protocols` version, so a user who tries to use this overlay in their configuration _may_ see a failure that looks like
```bash
$ nix build github:johnrichardrinehart/johnos/3272048990abebb8ae7f139fc286d1d56e7f05f7#nixosConfigurations.framework-laptop.pkgs.hyprland

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

title: Nix: using hyprland from overlays.default causes build failure
body:
1. clone this repo.
2. checkout `v0.25.0` tag.
3. run `nix repl`.
4. input the following expression:

```
(import inputs.nixpkgs { system = "x86_64-linux"; overlays = [ outputs.overlays.default ]; }).hyprland.buildInputs
```

We can easily find out, surprisingly, the `hyprland-protocols` dependency is using the package from nixpkgs (`«derivation /nix/store/rvjgyrq10fmjir672lkfql2cn1rqzkm5-hyprland-protocols-unstable-2023-01-13.drv»`), which will cause the build failure later, because:
https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/0432804b180dbdf7aed64a5bf71b912a937e2e04/protocols/meson.build#L8

I know this can be easily fixed by specifying the package in releavant callPackage function. However, the real problem is that we've used a lot of `self.overlays`. We should really consider wheels like flake-parts instead, or this kind of problems and infinite recursion will happen very frequently.

title: [Nvidia] Pipewire doesn't detect screens, most likely a portals issue
body:
I am aware Nvidia isn't natively supported.

I will mention as many details as possible and try to slowly rule out possible variables, please bear with me if the issue is too long. I will also try to keep it as systematic and clear as possible.

Before I discuss the issue, I want to brief you about my system and setup.

My desktop PC:- 1. Init System: OpenRC; 2. Distro: Gentoo; 3. GPU: Nvidia GTX 1650(proprietary 
drivers)

### Installing
 
I first went over the general installation of Hyprland on Gentoo, using the package available in wayland-desktop repository and enabled the required USE flags and keywords.

I have read through and implemented Nvidia-specific changes in my config file. I have also confirmed that I am running the proprietary driver and not the nouveau ones. Direct Rendering is enabled and functions normally.

I then installed Pipewire and Wireplumber as stated in the Gentoo Wiki https://wiki.gentoo.org/wiki/PipeWire . I also enabled the required USE flags (except GStreamer, I will update in the comments once I am done emerging my packages)

Keep in mind, flags like `system-service` aren't needed as this is an OpenRC system

I have installed xdg-desktop-portal and XDPH, also verifiying that -gnome and -kde ones don't exist. I have verified that -wlr never emerges either.

Installing Pipewire/Wireplumber also requires Pulseaudio-daemon to be removed, which I have done and verified that it never launches.

Grimblast is installed as well.
### Setting up

I use Chris Titus' (forked from linux mobile) configs, and added the following lines:

```
# portals
exec-once = ~/.config/hypr/xdg-portal-hyprland
exec-once = dbus-update-activation-environment --all WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP

# gentoo-specific stuff
exec-once = gentoo-pipewire-launcher &

#NVIDIA STUFF
env = LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME,nvidia
env = XDG_SESSION_TYPE,wayland
env = GBM_BACKEND,nvidia-drm
env = __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME,nvidia
env = WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS,1
```
Aside from these, some personal adjustments were made, but none that would affect portals or wireplumber stuff.

In addition to this, I added this to my DM's config

```

Comment=An intelligent dynamic tiling Wayland compositor
Exec=dbus-launch --exit-with-session Hyprland
Type=Application
```
This ensures Pipewire/Wireplumber have no issues with permissions of any sorts

### The Problem

I noticed that my screenshots are blank, OBS doesn't detect displays (even the flatpak one) and Screencasting on Firefox is also not functioning (I have verified that my about:config reflects pipewire usage). I have followed the Hyprland's Wiki for "Screenshare / OBS no worky"

**I don't get any windows from hyprland-share-picker** during the entirety of this process.

info: [pipewire] No captures available

I verified if Pipewire was even running in the first place

```
$ LANG=C pactl info | grep "Server Name"
Server Name: PulseAudio (on PipeWire 0.3.67)

1. Init System: SystemD; 2. Distro: Arch Linux; 3. GPU: Integrated Intel(non-Xe, don't recall exact names)

Apart from those above, everything else is practically the same as my desktop setup. Just that I run Zen kernel on the laptop

I have no such issues on this laptop. I still run Pipewire/Wireplumber on the laptop, I use OBS, I use Grimblast and Screensharing works well too.

### Theories And Speculation

As Gentoo's wiki doesn't give full information for setting up video sources for Pipewire/Wireplumber, it could be a point of failure. The logs of OBS also mention how sources weren't detected, indicating that it _might_ be incorrectly configured, but this is rather unlikely.

XDPH is probably not suited for my case. This is an edge case of a user running OpenRC, Gentoo, Nvidia with proprietary drivers and a Xanmod kernel. This is definately not a common setup and I can totally understand not having any foresight for this. It is a weird mix of things, and any of them are  potential points of failure.

Fortunately, one of the dudes in IRC who helped me out also ran a similar setup, they used an AMD GPU and SystemD instead. Same Gentoo and also ran Hyprland. They found the issue peculiar too.

### Closing Notes/ TL;DR

I want to investigate this issue and I am also willing to update the wiki about it if a fix is found.

I will also attach Hyprland log files [here](https://files.catbox.moe/sfahfs.log) if that helps.

More info will be provided upon request :3

title: Add split preselection
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
This adds the bspwm like preselection in case you want your window to open in a specific direction.
Note this only works for Dwindle.

#### Changes
added a persistent mode: permanent_direction_override
this leaves the  selected direction until: another direction has been specified, no direction has been specified (any other character as direction as those who would specify a direction), or this mode is turned off in config.

config entry is in dwindle -> dwindle:permanent_direction_override

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
I am not a user of groups, and or special workspaces, so if there are issues with them please tell me.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
It should be ready for merging, a quick look at the impl is ofc appreciated.


#### Usage
hyprctl dispatch layoutmsg "preselect u"  -> up (or t)
hyprctl dispatch layoutmsg "preselect d" -> down (or b)
hyprctl dispatch layoutmsg "preselect r" -> right
hyprctl dispatch layoutmsg "preselect l" -> left
hyprctl dispatch layoutmsg "preselect n" -> no direction (this can be any character other than those above)
the no direction is needed to reset the override in persistent mode.


wiki entry: https://github.com/hyprwm/hyprland-wiki/pull/218
implements: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/836

title: renderer,config: add custom DRM modeline support
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

This allows specifying custom display resolutions for the DRM backend. This is useful for display overclocking, working around broken EDIDs, etc. To use this feature, specify a modeline instead of a resolution in the config, for example:

```
monitor = DP-1, modeline 1071.101 3840 3848 3880 3920 2160 2263 2271 2277 +hsync -vsync, 0x0, 1
```

This example is a custom 3840x2160@120Hz mode with tightened timings. I use it because the standard timings don't work with my monitor and GPU combination (M28U with RX580).

The syntax is compatible with Sway and Xorg.


#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I've been daily driving this for a few weeks and haven't ran into any issues.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

I think it is, but probably needs a documentation update as well.

title: existing workspace rules are not replaced when adding new ones

When redefining a workspace rule, the old one will have precedence over the new one since the new one is added at the back of the deque, instead of modifying the exiting one.

for instance:
`hyprctl keyword workspace 8,monitor:DP-9`
`hyprctl keyword workspace 8,monitor:eDP-1`

one would expect that workspace 8 would open on eDP-1 but it opens on DP-9

title: Reaper Constant Re-focusing Within The Main Window
body:
Hi, sorry to bother you with the legacy X11 stuff, but i really like Hyprland and switched to it as a daily driver. Everything works great except for Reaper(of course lol).  I use Reaper as my main audio production tool and rely on it at the studio. Unfortunately there are no news from the Reaper devs about making it Wayland ready so i was hoping that we could try to get it ironed out a bit.
 As a couple of users before mentioned before that Sway seemed to had all those things too but they fixed them in the git version.

 I could see that the menu bug was fixed, but there is one with the pop-up windows and the constant refocusing one.

The pop-up window bug:
 Initially when i tried to use Reaper, the following would happen: anytime i would open a patch menu or a plugin, it would spawn a small popup window on the top of the main window(with the plugin or something similar) the window would be focused. As i start moving the mouse way from the button and towards  the window it would close itself.
 I found a fix for this by using these window rules together:   **follow_mouse=1    mouse_refocus=false**  
I don't know if it's a good fix but it seemed to have fixed the the popup disappearing problem.

The refocus bug:
This one is the most annoying: when you hover over buttons(mute, solo etc), sliders(faders) and other elements within the main window, the main window keeps constantly going in and out of focus. It seems like Hyprland thinks that each of those elements is a separate window so it keeps shifting the focus away from the min window. This causes slowness, when you work fast the mouse clicks on faders or pan wheels  don't register(or refocus) fast enough and you end up missing and there's no "fader grab action" happening so you end up dragging nothing. Sway on the other hand doesn't exhibit that behavior and the main window stays focused at all times and there's no lag and actuation misses mentioned above. 

   I don't know how useful is the Sway comparison, but it would seem like there should be a simple fix for this...
Lmk what you guys think, any help would be greatly appreciated!

title: fullscreen field not respected in windowrulev2
body:
**NOTE: This does not crash Hyprland.  Just an invalid behavior.** 

### Steps to reproduce
I wanted to make my terminal transparent and everything else opaque. So i changed the opacity variables to 1 and made an window rule for my terminal:
```
decoration {
    active_opacity = 1
    inactive_opacity = 1
    fullscreen_opacity = 1
}
windowrulev2 = opacity 0.9 0.9, class:^(kitty)$
```
This works fine *except when the terminal is fullscreen*. So i added the the `fullscreen` field to the windowrules:
```
windowrulev2 = opacity 0.9 0.9, class:^(kitty)$, fullscreen:1
windowrulev2 = opacity 0.9 0.9, class:^(kitty)$, fullscreen:0
```
According to the [wiki](https://wiki.hyprland.org/Configuring/Window-Rules/#window-rules-v2) this should work, but it does not. I checked with other fields, **every other fields are working fine, even `fullscreen: 0` works fine** but `fullscreen:1`  does not seem to have any effect.

### Expected outcome
kitty should be transparent even when made fullscreen.

### Noted outcome
kitty is not transparent when made fullscreen, `fullscreen: 1` does not have any effect.

title: Fix not finding function symbols for hooking
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Fixes #2177.

Adds a new `execAndGet` function that puts its STDERR into the log to make it more discoverable when child processes fail. This also fixes not being able to run `nm` on the hyprland binary if the path contains spaces.

Wraps the nix binary to include `binutils` (`nm`) as function symbols were missing because it was not in path.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
There may or may not be a C++ stdlib function that actually implements child process pipes. I was not able to find it if there is.
I'm fairly sure every case in `execAndGet` is handled, including exceptions, but there may be something I missed.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
I have tested it, and it's ready if you have no issues with the implementation.

title: `focusmonitor +1` won't refocus a window after `movewindow, mon:+1`
body:
Pretty minor issue.

On a two monitor setup, with Dwindle layout, using a keybind for `movewindow, mon:+1` on e.g. workspace 1, when switching back to the previous monitor with `focusmonitor +1` no window is focused on that workspace. Doing pretty much anything other than `focusmonitor +1` again on workspace 1 focuses a window back.

Edit: Just to add, this seems to be related to when a split is "unsplit" and the focus goes to another monitor, this makes what may be the "last window" information point to a now not-present window. This also happens in some swallowing cases.

title: make split preselect available in config file

I did change DwindleLayout.cpp so that it will split arguments on ',' instead of ' ', so you can use the "layoutmsg" dispatcher with comma separated arguments instead of space separated ones. Ready for merging

title: Fix broken pipe crash when event listener terminates
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Fixes a case where hyprland can crash due to a broken IPC pipe.

Here's how to reproduce it:
```bash
socat -d -d -d -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:/tmp/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | (while read -r line; do echo "$line"; kill -SIGINT 0; done)
```

Open two windows.  Run that in one.  Change focus (or generate any other IPC event).

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
This is a race between https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/5627b70981730cf1839ae4477f9fd086d4fc7a6c/src/managers/EventManager.cpp#L27 and https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/5627b70981730cf1839ae4477f9fd086d4fc7a6c/src/managers/EventManager.cpp#L111

The array that keeps track of the FDs does eventually get cleaned up, and maybe this catch block should clean it up immediately, but ignoring it seems ok too.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Ready for merging.

title: Monitors: Refer Monitors with hardware-related identifiers
body:
# Current Functionality
In the config, monitors are referred by the graphic output's ID (e.g. eDP-1)

# Problem and Use Case
As the currently used Identifier usually identifies the output port, but not the monitor itself, configuration for different hardware setups that can be connected to the computer at different times cannot be configured easily.

In my case, I  use my Notebook with three different hardware setups. Two of those are docking stations at different working desks, where different monitors (two each) are present with different desired arrangement and resolutions.
However, on both setups, the IDs of the two monitors are DP-5 and DP-6.
Hence, I cannot configure the individual setups in Hyprland.

# Possible Solution
My proposal is to provide an option to identify the monitors via the EDID fields yielded by `hyprctl monitors`.
Maybe, use an approach similar to window-rulesv2 and call this *monitor-rules*, where arbitrary EDID fields (and maybe a field called `output` or `id` for the old identifier)  may be referred.

A monitor configuration might then be have the form:
`monitorv2=serial:J8J313CPAJ2L,1920x1080@60.000000,2560x0,1`

title: Add hyprland to waybar-hyprland path as fallback for hyprctl
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
In some environments, such as using the [home-manager waybar module's systemd integration](https://github.com/nix-community/home-manager/blob/master/modules/programs/waybar.nix#L198), hyprctl may not be in `PATH`. As a result, waybar crashes when attempting to call out to hyprctl to get information for eg. the currently active workspace.

This PR adds a wrapper to the waybar binary, appending hyprctl to `PATH`. This allows waybar to use the current environment's hyprctl, if one exists, and falls back to the default hyprland package if there is none.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
This might not be the most efficient way to do this, as it always pulls the `hyprland` derivation no matter what the user is actually using. People using patched versions of hyprland (eg. `hyprland-nvidia`) would end up pulling two copies of Hyprland into the store. While (to my knowledge) this shouldn't break anything in waybar, this does result in a potentially unnecessary copy of Hyprland being added to the store. I'm open to suggestions on improving this.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Assuming the caveat I described above is fine, this should be ready to merge.

title: movefocus broken.
body:
Since a few commits movefocus doesn't work anymore for me. 
Sometimes it's possible to use it once, after that there is no effect at all for any direction.

title: Resize window after ungrouping a single window group
body: ungrouping a group of 1 window doesn't change the window size to fill the space previously occupied by the group indicator bar.

title: Allow for Ignoring all Keybinds if Rules are Met
body: I wish a window rule be added which will make it ignore any keybinds. This can be useful for RDP software where the remote system uses same keybinds as the local system. So you could add a rule that says "If X app is Fullscreend, ignore keybinds".

title: Android Studio tooltips taking focus
body: Tooltips in android studio are taking focus away from the android studio window.  This is a new issue that appeared to me in that past couple weeks.

body:
Hi, 

This is a very basic PR to be able to get an event only when a window title change. (active and inactive windows)

This will allow me to refresh https://github.com/hyprland-community/hyprland-autoname-workspaces on title update.

Also, hyprland-rs PR is ready for this: https://github.com/hyprland-community/hyprland-rs/pull/56/files

I don't understand/know if we need also to add a `EMIT_HOOK_EVENT("windowTitle", PWINDOW);`

Should I ?

title: Screen freezes randomly
body:
When logging into hyprland, randomly the screen will freeze and no updates to the screen are visible. Sometimes this happens a few minutes after startup, sometimes there is not a problem all day. I'm still able to interact with the system. I'm able to kill Hyprland or reboot the system by mimicking the key presses I would normally use, however, nothing changes on the screen. No terminal pops up and the mouse doesn't move. Running this on arcolinux (arch derivative). Attached is the hyprland log file 
[hyprlandLog.txt](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/files/11641938/hyprlandLog.txt), the crash report
[hyprlandCrashReport2792.txt](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/files/11641947/hyprlandCrashReport2792.txt), and my config file 
[hyprland.txt](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/files/11641955/hyprland.txt).


Not sure if the crash report is referring to when I am forced to exit Hyprland. Therefore, coredumpctl does not give any PIDs for me to post the info of.  Please let me know if I can provide any more information. I switched from the linux-lts kernel to the standard linux kernel before writing this. So far, it seems as if there has been no freezing issues, however, as I mentioned the freezing happens at random it seems.

title: Add hot corner functionality
body:
Hot corners would be a small but useful addition to Hyprland. The idea is that an action occurs when the mouse is moved into a specific corner of the desktop for a certain amount of time (e.g. 200ms), with or without specified modifier keys.

I am only aware of it being implemented on MacOS, but the functions you can assign to it there are very limited so it can only be more potent on Hyprland.

Some functions which are useful to assign to the corners are to run an app launcher, activate a screen locker, toggle a special workspace, cycle through workspaces, or run really any command relevant to a certain workflow.

The overall effect of this feature is that it gives the mouse considerably more power to activate functions in the desktop environment.
This video demonstrates the concept briefly: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PaxFUybMbng

title: Make movetoworkspace register previous workspace
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
`movetoworkspace` didn't register previous workspace so there was no way to go back to previous workspace by using `workspace, previous` even if `binds/allow_workspace_cycles` is enabled.

Fixed it such that `movetoworkspace` will update the previous workspace if `binds/allow_workspace_cycles` is enabled.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
No.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Ready to merge.

title: Fix fractional scale updates in some cases
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

The fractional scale of windows was not updated on "keyboard" moves (`movecurrentworkspacetomonitor` and `movetoworkspace` if the target workspace is on a different monitor), while it worked as expected when dragging a window with the mouse. Similar to https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/1794. Although that issue was already fixed, I am observing the same behavior on current `main`.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

This is my first time doing anything with Hyprland (or even Wayland for that matter), so not sure if I did it right.

In `CWindow::moveToWorkspace()`, the scale used appears to be the one from the previous monitor (where the window used to be), but I'm not sure if there are any unintended side-effects from setting `m_iMonitorID`. If that is bad, the scaling behavior was also fixed by only creating `PMONITOR` from `PWORKSPACE->m_iMonitorID`.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

Apart from the above disclaimer, I think it's ready (for what it's worth). I tested it with two monitors of different scale (2.0 and 1.6), and alacritty as client.

title: Add support for matching monitors by serial number
body:
The reason for this is that for people such as me who "share" monitors between different machines (whether it be with an HDMI switch or plug/unplug), the DP of the monitors that are being switched changes after every plug/unplug, which makes it impossible to configure their position and any other related option that requires a DP number.

My middle monitor, DP-3, is being toggled to display either my  linux or windows machine. Everytime it gets toggled to windows and then back to linux, its DP changes. DP-3 -> DP-5 -> DP->7 etc..

title: noborder creates transparent borders
body:
I'm trying to remove borders for firefox nightly like this (10 for easy inspection):

```
general {
    border_size = 10
}

windowrule = noborder,^(firefox-nightly)$
```

But there is still a 10-pixel border around firefox, just transparent. (For transparent borders, one can just set border_color to a transparent color.)

I want firefox to be really noborder due to fractional scale issues. Firefox can do fraction scale by setting `widget.wayland.fractional_buffer_scale` to the scale value in `about:config`. But with scale=1.25 and border_size=1, it means Firefox window starts at (1.25, 1.25) which isn't a whole pixel, making text blurry. Setting border_size=1.25 doesn't seem to work, and setting to 4 is too large.

(This doesn't affect programs that properly support fractional scale e.g. alacritty.)

#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
- This PR allows setting an alpha value for layer surface blur ignoring, instead of only ignoring fully transparent pixels
- Why? Because it helps reduce weird glowing anti-aliased pixels of rounded elements (in waybar/eww/etc.)
- How? `layerrule = ignorealpha, NAMESPACE`. Both "ignorealpha" and "ignorezero" work.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
- This feature works when configured correctly, but no logging is made when an invalid value (not a float) is given to the rule

title: feat: add lockactivegroup dispatcher
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

The `lockactivewindow` dispatcher takes `lock`, `toggle` or `unlock` as arguments. When a group is locked, no window or group can be added to it, nor can it be added to another group, but the `moveintogroup` and `moveoutofgroup` dispatches are not affected. Has no effect on non-group.

#### Implementation details:

the lock is implement via `SGroupData.locked` flag (defaults to false).

The flag is only relevant to the group head, and upon the group head's succession, the flag will be passed down to the new head. Meanwhile, the old head's flag will be set to false.

The flag is set to false when a group is dismissed.

New condition checks have been added to the dwindle and master layout to check if target group is unlocked (and if the source is also a group and unlocked) before adding windows to the target group.

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?

tested locally.

title: Poor performance when focus changes
body:
Setup: 

Arch Linux
hyprland-git `r2982.e1edfde5-1`
i9-11900H CPU/GPU
4k60 display

Steps to repro:
Enable the debug overlay
Open two windows
Switch focus

Result:
Watch FPS drop significantly for a few seconds

Expected result:
FPS maintains constant 60Hz

Additional info:
It seems to be bound on the GPU here, but I don't think it's maxxing out the GPU...looking at intel_gpu_top, when spamming focus changes, GPU usage is around 88%, but for some reason it's only running at 500 MHz, with a max stated as ~1500MHz--so it seems like the GPU isn't clocking up correctly or something like that?

When just sitting on a desktop running a Firefox instance, intel_gpu_top and htop in terminals, Hyprland uses ~38% CPU (htop numbers, so 100% means ONE core fully utilized). When spamming switching focus, it goes down to 10%, likely b/c waiting on the GPU. 

It seems like switching focus shouldn't be such a GPU intensive task, and it seems like my system has the headroom to work much nicer if the GPU were able to clock up properly. 

Given the GPU clocking stuff, this may be a driver bug of sorts, or at least partially?

In general performance on this 4k display is pretty poor with this GPU, and it's pretty smooth in Windows and it's very smooth running 1x 1440p60 + 1x 1440p144, which is more pixels per second, so something particular to the 4k case seems to be happening? 

Maybe related to https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/2305 also

title: next workspace on an output
body:
I'd like to identify all workspaces on an output and cycle between them.  Basically reproducing i3's `workspace next_on_output` and `workspace prev_on_output` commands.

I think a good starting place for this might be to include an additional key in the `monitors` query for hyprctl for Workspaces.  Currently it reports the active workspace, but I have not found a way to identify all the other ones on the same output to script this.  Is there already a way to do this by chance?

Apologies for asking what is basically a question, but I suppose if it's not possible I'd like to suggest it as a feature.  I'm just not sure and could use some help.

Also thanks for the really cool window manager!

title: Plugin config values stay as default until end of PLUGIN_INIT
body:
I've noticed that config values created whit HyprlandAPI::addConfigValue keep their default value in PLUGIN_INIT and in all functions called directly from PLUGIN_INIT. I'm not sure if this is the intended behavior or not, but I've seen plugins made by others also make the assumption that it should work. They work fine when called from functions triggered by events or in PLUGIN_EXIT.

How to reproduce:

1. Set the value in config:

`plugin {`
`    foo {`
`        bar=something`
`    }`
`}`

2. Do this inside of PLUGIN_INIT:

`HyprlandAPI::addConfigValue(PHANDLE, "plugin:foo:bar", SConfigValue{.strValue = STRVAL_EMPTY});`
`HyprlandAPI::reloadConfig();`
`HyprlandAPI::addNotification(PHANDLE, g_pConfigManager->getConfigValuePtrSafe("plugin:foo:bar")->strValue, CColor{0.f, 1.f, 1.f, 1.f}, 5000);`

title: Hyprland doesn't start on Mesa 23.1.2 on OpenSUSE Tumbleweed
body:
After updating my Mesa drivers to 23.1.2, Hyprland will not start. Log gives the error `[CRITICAL] m_sWLRRenderer is NULL!`. 

Rolling back my system to before the update via a btrfs snapshot, Hyprland works fine.

This behaviour occurs with both drivers from the official openSUSE repos and the Packman repos, on both Hyprland built from source (i.e. the git version) and Hyprland from the openSUSE repos.

My config file: https://pastebin.com/7yXrsaY3 (pretty close to the default, so I doubt this is an issue)
Hyprland crash report: https://pastebin.com/iXcttDNZ

title: Invalid keyboard layout passed
body:
That is the error I started getting with my first boot of my day today. Everything has been working for months up until now. I haven't played around or even touched my settings as well.

- Steps to reproduce
```
input {
    kb_layout = dvorak
    kb_options = caps:backspace
}
```
`localectl set-keymap dvorak` and `loadkeys dvorak` do not do anything either.

It is also worth noting that I tried a few other generic layouts. The only two that worked were 'us' and 'de'??? 'Azerty' and 'uk' do not work for example...

-  Noted outcome

Hyprland defaults back to (us) qwerty. Consequently, this issue took me 15 minutes to create because I forgot most of my qwerty muscle memory. Free me from this pain :(

title: Screenshots and screensharing both broken on scaled+rotated display
body:
Confused as I used to be able to screenshot. Running an RX570. Rendering is normal it is just screenshots and screensharing that are broken.

Normal config for all the monitors:

```
monitor=,preferred,auto,1
monitor=DP-1,highres,1080x400,2,bitdepth,10
monitor=DP-3,preferred,0x0,2
monitor=HDMI-A-1,preferred,3000x0,1
monitor=DP-3,transform,3
monitor=HDMI-A-1,transform,1
```
monitors were both moved (in the X axis) and scaled when I mention that the displays were scaled (to keep them contiguous)

![allnormalscaling](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/assets/59203114/7890ac11-f4f1-4471-a54b-ed861a0e2201)
^ All displays with their preferred resolution and scale set to 1x (left and middle are 4k, right is 1080p)

![leftscaled](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/assets/59203114/81a41eb6-4fd7-4c9f-9f76-350b32aba5d9)
^ Only the left monitor scaled to 2x

![leftmiddlescaled](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/assets/59203114/ce6b4b59-9d6d-4faf-b2da-f90f27043a40)
^ Both the left and middle monitor scaled to 2x

All of the screenshots were taken using `grim -`. 

Attempting to record the screens via `wf-recorder` appear to have the same results as the screenshots. i.e. left display is cut off, middle display is completely black (wf-recorder also **always** says `Application provided invalid, non monotonically increasing dts to muxer in stream 0:` when recording this display) , right display works perfectly.

title: Fix crash when screen size is 0x0
body:
Fix crash when screen size is 0x0 (When booting into laptop clam mode in dell XPS)
and also ignore any screen with size 0x0 in the first place

# Crash fix
When I boot into clam mode (lid is closed) on my laptop, the laptop screen is recognized as size 0x0.
Hyprland starts normally and treats it as a regular screen (which i cannot use of course).
Then I can crash it in two ways:
1. Try to disable the monitor (to move all workspaces to the external monitor)
2. Switch to a workspace on the laptop monitor, and close a window.

I get the following error:
```
ASSERTION FAILED! 

cannot alloc a FB with negative / zero size! (attempted 0x0)

at: line 6 in Framebuffer.cpp
```

## Additional work
Since there is no point in using a 0x0 screen,  listener_newOutput will ignore such screens

title: Plugin: getting data from a monitor (g_pCompositor->m_vMonitors) throws segfault
body:
I'm using this plugin: https://github.com/Duckonaut/split-monitor-workspaces

Since [this commit](fbabb105c3427fbbce4dfc3ea9701ba473298206), accessing data from a monitor ([example](https://github.com/Duckonaut/split-monitor-workspaces/blob/main/src/main.cpp#L67)) crashes Hyprland entirely. Even just printing `std::cout << monitor << std::endl;` will crash it.

### Steps to reproduce:

1. Checkout this commit: fbabb105c3427fbbce4dfc3ea9701ba473298206
2. Use a plugin that accesses `g_pCompositor->m_vMonitors`, and make it access one of the monitors
3. Start Hyprland with the default config. Load the plugin in the config, or manually through hyprctl plugin load.

### Expected outcome
The plugin should work the same as it does with the parent commit fbabb105c3427fbbce4dfc3ea9701ba473298206

### Noted outcome
The plugin crashes Hyprland when loading the plugin.

### Log
(from a nested debug build of that commit, running through vscode)

title: "Communication with the local password server failed" when using Dolphin
body:
An issue I am having with Dolphin, the KDE file manager, is seen whenever I attempt to connect to a network share that has credentials stored presumably in KDE Wallet.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open Dolphin
2. Connect to a network share (SMB, SFTP, FTP...) that requires authentication
A Samba share with locked folders works too.
3. "Communication with the local password server failed" appears, at which point it has entirely failed to ask the user to authenticate at all.

The CLI outputs this:
```
kf.kio.core: Can't communicate with kiod_kpasswdserver (for queryAuthInfo)!
kf.kio.core: "Communication with the local password server failed"
```
...whereas the expected outcome is for it to communicate with Wallet, fetch the credentials in there and let the user carry on unabated.

I'm unsure if it's a KDE issue or a Hyprland issue, but I figured I might as well share it here.
Seems as though there is some miscommunication between KDE and Wallet, which is something I have also noticed with other things (like certain apps such as Steam and Flatpak apps not opening the file select dialog).

title: Black bars on latest Nvidia drivers 535.54.03-1
body:
# Issue
Updating to the latest version (535.54.03-1) of the nvidia-dkms package on Arch produces moving horizontal black bars on the screen. 

Downgrading to 530.41.03-1 fixes it.

title: [force_zero_scaling] Mouse location not correctly detected outside of the top left quadrant on force_zero_scaling
body:
When using force_zero_scaling on Hyprland (latest build), my mouse cursor is "bound" to the top left quadrant of my screen. The cursor itself moves beyond that, but it's location is capped at halfway along the screen horizontally and vertically.

My monitor resolution is 2880 by 1800, although xrandr lists this as 1440 by 900 (which I would imagine is what causes the issue?).

This issue occurs in Steam, Spotify, Minecraft and every other xwayland application I have tested.

title: Fullscreening all windows inside a split
body:
This is bit hard to describe, so I'm attaching a visual here. I'm a former herbstluftwm user and one bit of functionality that I miss from it is the ability to have a document I'm working with maximized to one side of the screen, while being able to toggle between multiple documents that are maximized to the opposite side. Again, hard to explain, so here's a visual mock-up I made of what it would look like in Hyprland:

![SplitScreenMockup](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/assets/3809531/88e9f285-33ea-4793-ad90-8ed0a13c9137)

As you can see, the notes document remains maximized on the left side of the split and the user is able to work in it while flipping between the multiple windows on the right. Herbstluftwm accomplishes this through a combination of a static split and fake-fullscreen behavior that fullscreens all the documents on the right to the dimensions of the right-hand split.

To be clear, I have read elsewhere here that Hyprland has no plans to implement static splits and that's fine. I'm merely wondering if there's a way to achieve the same effect with the current dynamic-split functionality. Perhaps it's already implemented and I've not fully understood the documentation — if so I would love someone to point the way to what I've missed. Otherwise, I would love it if some version of this functionality could be implemented.

Many thanks, either way.

title: hyprland very poor gaming performance
Avoid passing unix socket descriptors to children
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Add FD_CLOEXEC flags to the server-side connection FDs to make them closed during exec-family functions execution.

STR:
1. Initiate a new terminal window
2. Spawn event command reader:
```
nc -U /tmp/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock
```
3. Initiate one more window
4. Type the following commands in it [3]:

```
$ lsof /tmp/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket{2,}.sock 2>/dev/null| grep $$
bash      1061789 hyprland-test   36u  unix 0x000000004aaa7091      0t0 18495726 /tmp/hypr/8407a9af0a333ade66d4deff7ef654a4594fe58f_1688619429/.socket.sock type=STREAM (LISTEN)
bash      1061789 hyprland-test   44u  unix 0x000000001fe46f8c      0t0 18493131 /tmp/hypr/8407a9af0a333ade66d4deff7ef654a4594fe58f_1688619429/.socket2.sock type=STREAM (LISTEN)
bash      1061789 hyprland-test   79u  unix 0x0000000072ffe8f2      0t0 18493151 /tmp/hypr/8407a9af0a333ade66d4deff7ef654a4594fe58f_1688619429/.socket2.sock type=STREAM (CONNECTED)
```
As you can see bash instance (pid=1061789) has retrieved FDs from Hyprland, even the connection socket that was initiated in [2].

5. Try to make some dirt using instance [3]:
```
$ echo fakemsg 1>&79
```
6. Check the instance [2]:
```activewindow>>Alacritty,hyprland-test:~
activewindowv2>>7f0bcc538f20
>>>>fakemsg<<<<
windowtitle>>7f0bcc538f20
activewindowv2>>7f0bcc538f20
activewindow>>Alacritty,hyprland-test:~
activewindow>>Alacritty,hyprland-test:~
activewindowv2>>7f0bcf4f2700
```

So currently any child could access Hyprland-side descriptors and even accept inbound connections to command and event sockets.

title: Add support for smart splitting
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

Imagine a square or rectangular box. Picture two diagonal lines crossing each other to form an 'X' that divides the box into four equal sections or triangles. Each triangle is an equal quarter of the box.

This PR adds support for splitting depending on which section the mouse cursor is currently over. Personally, I find this slightly more intuitive.

A new configuration option has been added `dwindle:smart_split`, which has to be set to `1` in order for this functionality to be enabled.

title: Allow floating windows under tiled windows
body:
So, I'm trying to replicate aspects of my config from KDE on Hyprland, and everything is coming along nicely. Except that I used to have Cava inside a terminal, positioned to cover the bottom half of my screen, and have it be under all windows.

I managed to get everything I wanted using window rules (and some aspects of it even better than with KDE's window rules):
```conf
windowrulev2 = float,          class:(kitty),title:(cava)

title: movewindow and resizewindow do not bring floating windows on top.
body:
Neither movewindow nor resizewindow bring **floating** window on top when used.
Instead, the window stays under other floating windows.
You need to left click window once, and then perform action and the window will be on top.

The window will become topmost in the floating window stack, and then it'll start moving/resizing

# Move/resize windows with mainMod + LMB/RMB and dragging
bindm = $mainMod, mouse:272, movewindow
bindm = $mainMod, mouse:273, resizewindow
```

title: swayidle stopped working, compositor doesnt implement protocol
body:
temporary fix: *roll back swayidle too 1.8.0*

started talking about this in discord, figured id open a bug report too
i updated my system sometime in the last month and i finally noticed yesterday that swayidle stopped working, looking through swayidles commits the only change  was dropping KDEs idle protocol in favor of the native wayland protocol

so i did some digging, and if im understanding the Hyprland code properly its using the dropped kde protocol instead of idle_notify-v1

wlroots/types/wlr_idle.c               <---- old kde protocol
wlroots/types/wlr_idle_notify.c   <---- new protocol

wl-roots still has a 8month old pr too drop support for it but
"
We might want to wait a bit for this. In the past we've waited a bit, then removed the protocol from Sway, then waited a bit, then removed the protocol from wlroots. Removing from wlroots impacts all compositors.
That said, this protocol has few clients, so might be able to go faster than usual.
"

title: Make bind modifiers case-insensitive
body:
Hyprland is very lenient when it comes to modifiers: `SUPERSHIFT`, `SUPER + SHIFT`, and `_xSUPERfoobarSHIFTx_` are all treated equally, but  `SUPER + shift` is treated as `SUPER`.

Thus, the config line

    bind = $mod + shift, T,       exec, notify-send Hello

unexpectedly binds notify-send to `$mod` not `$mod + SHIFT`. No warning is printed.

This PR makes modifiers case-insensitive. It has been tested and is ready to be merged.

Feel free to close this, if you don't like the change.

title: Double fractional scaling for dpi-aware apps
body:
The foot terminal emulator recently implemented fractional scaling.  With two monitors of different physical dimensions and hyprland set to scale them each at 1.0, foot now changes its font size to look identical on each screen - but other apps are too small as they can't do this trick.

If hyprland is set to scale the physically smaller monitor higher than 1.0, it appears that both foot and hyprland apply scaling and it ends up too big.

I am not sure if it's possible for hyprland or foot, or any other wayland app, to be aware of eachothers' dpi awareness capabilities, but it would be cool to be able to run in a mixed mode where the compositor is scaling apps that are not dpi-aware while apps that can do it on their own are allowed to do so.

title: Avoid connected monitor reusing unavailable ID
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?

@ti-mo noticed a bug in my previous PR: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/pull/2666#issuecomment-1637994116, where two monitors might get the same ID. This PR aims to fix this bug. 

The problem seems to happen when you have 2 monitors connected, and the monitor ID map looks something like this:

```jsonc
{
  DP-2 = 0 // connected
  DP-3 = 1 // connected
}
```
Disconnecting DP-2 and plugging it into DP-1 would give it ID=0 and update the map like this:
```jsonc
{
  DP-1 = 0 // connected
  DP-2 = 0 // disconnected
  DP-3 = 1 // connected
}
```
Then, disconnecting DP-3 and plugging it into DP-2 would still give it ID=0:
```jsonc
{
  DP-1 = 0 // connected
  DP-2 = 0 // connected
  DP-3 = 1 // disconnected
}
```

This PR fixes this, by checking whether no other currently connected monitor is using this ID. If it is, it will pick the next available ID. The last situtation would then look like this instead:
```jsonc
{
  DP-1 = 0 // connected
  DP-2 = 1 // connected
  DP-3 = 1 // disconnected
}
```

Maybe there's a better way to fix this, but I can't think of anything right now.


#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

I couldn't reproduce the bug but I believe this will fix it. @ti-mo Can you verify this?

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Needs to be tested just to be sure. I saw no problems with my own tests, but couldn't reproduce the issue before my changes.

My config for fullscreen is: `bind = $mod, F, fullscreen, 0` (I just added the ending 0, to no avail)

title: Power draw due to inefficiency
body:
### Hyprland Version

7c1dacea09e18ddf74fcb9e0be2debce9c0cf94d dirty (only return 0 when using -h (2738)). Tag: v0.27.0-26-g7c1dacea

### Bug or Regression?

Bug

### Description

Sorry to bring up this topic 
but if I watch a random video (YT or some other streaming page, tested in Firefox) 
when I compare the `intel-gpu-top` and `nvtop` outputs I get the following characteristics

1. Picture Gnome on the left, Hyprland (0.27 tag or latest commit doesn't change anything) on the right
2. Picture Sway-git

![image](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/assets/5576250/8e6f2270-0732-4cf0-a2c8-069ee749ca11)
![image](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/assets/5576250/333c2c90-da33-4895-aa2e-714943e357f8)

Gnome 1.7/23.0 W
Hyprland 11.8/30.6 W
Sway 2.5/21.7 W

Furthermore, it can be seen that Hyprland transfers much more data to the memory (via IMC) 
Gnome | read 3.3GB | write 1.6GB
Hyprland | read 9.6GB |write 7GB
Sway | read 5GB | write 4GB

### How to reproduce

Just watch a video and choose a defined  resolution (1080) and make sure that your GPU supports hardware acceleration for the file codec (should be visible in intel_gpu_top under video or in nvtop under  ENC/DEC[   0%]).

The same video draws much more power under Hyprland and transfers much more data (and has higher GPU%) as in the other "Display Managers".

Bug

title: Hyprland not launching after kernel and package update
body:
### Hyprland Version

both latest commit and 0.27.1

### Bug or Regression?

Regression

### Description

After updating the kernel (`linux` and `linux-zen`) and the `hyprland-git` package from AUR, Hyprland fails to launch. I noticed a similar behavior when attempting to use NVIDIA drivers and the GPU as the primary graphics card. However, reverting to integrated GPU with the non-patched version allowed Hyprland to run and haven't had any problems since then. Other applications are working correctly on my system after the updates.

**Steps Taken to Solve the Problem:**
1. Installed the LTS kernel to check if the issue was kernel-related.
2. Tried using both NVIDIA proprietary drivers and `nouveau`, but the problem persisted in both cases.
3. Removed the `hyprland-git` package from AUR and installed `hyprland` from official repositories.
4. Attempted to build Hyprland from source, but the issue remained.

There must be something I'm missing for sure. I couldn't get to write the output of Hyprland command from TTY to a file, sometimes it stops at a `seatd` error or sometimes at `Found 1 GPUs`. Please let me know if there's anything helpful I can provide.

### How to reproduce

1. Update the kernel to the latest version (`linux 6.4.4` and `linux-zen 6.4.4` or `linux-lts 6.1.139`).
2. Update the `hyprland-git` package from AUR (or install `hyprland` package from official repo).
3. Attempt to launch Hyprland (simply reboot).

title: Misuse of IPC socket causes Hyprland to lock up
body:
### Hyprland Version

Bug

Attempting to read from .socket.sock via `socat` (say, for example, you got the direction wrong and typed `-U` instead of `-u`) causes Hyprland to lock up until the socket is closed.

While I get that at some level this is a "play dumpass games, win dumpass prizes" type of thing, Hyprland probably shouldn't lock up to the point I need to ssh in from my phone and kill some processes to get it to respond again.

4. SSH in from another computer and `killall socat`

title: dwindle: add config option to enable/disable new intuitive resizing
body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
- #2681 is cool, but I prefer the old resizing behaviour. In the below example, dragging the top-right corner of window 2 doesn't do anything
```
  | 2
1 +---
  | 3 
```
- This PR adds the config option `dwindle:smart_resizing`, which enables the new resizing behaviour if set to `1` and disables otherwise. Enabled by default.

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)
- Literally copied the old code and put it in an if-else

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
- If you think just using the old resizing code is acceptable, at least for now until the new resizing behaviour gets improved

title: animations:enabled=false is ignored during startup since v0.25.0
body:
### Hyprland Version

v0.27.2-32-g375e8385

### Bug or Regression?

Regression

### Description

Regressed by ddfeebad3dea. When Hyprland is started the applications run immediately on startup have zoom out animation even if disabled in config. This can be distracting and interfere with benchmarking or nesting under another compositor. For example, parent Hyprland may *not* want child Hyprland instances to animate fullscreen content within.

Workaround: prepend `sleep 2 && ` to `exec` or `exec-once` to add minor delay


### How to reproduce

```
$ cat /tmp/hyprland.conf
animations:enabled = false
exec-once = glmark2-wayland -b build && hyprctl dispatch exit 0

$ Hyprland -c /tmp/hyprland.conf
```


### Crash reports, logs, images, videos

_No response_

title: Fix for issue #2797
body:
Fixes issue https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/issues/2797

There was some weird issue with setting the priority to realtime before calling g_pCompositor initserver that was making wlroots very unhappy resulting in a crash in some instances.

Also some params were being lost by not reading the current params then modifying the priority and instead creating new params with only a priority.

title: Hyprland takes a long time to start
body:
### Hyprland Version

Hyprland, built from branch main at commit f5913135c638997f8c13a52d0760803947ae3889 dirty (input: add support for cursor-shape-v1). Tag: v0.27.2-51-gf5913135

### Bug or Regression?

Regression

### Description

Hyprland usually launches within 2-3 seconds, but sometimes it takes up to 2 minutes, this happens roughly 10% of the time. Has been happening on -git for at least 3 weeks.
Same thing also applies for exiting Hyprland. The longer start only happens on the first start of Hyprland per boot. But exiting Hyprland takes more time on all subsequent instances of Hyprland. 

### How to reproduce

1. boot into tty
2. launch Hyprland
3. repeat till the launch takes considerably longer

title: [Query] What is the Hyprland equivalent of `Environment=DISPLAY=:0` ?
body:
I am looking into documenting laptop stuff for Hyprland. For this case, i want the session to lock when the lid is closed.

This can be achieved in a few ways, but 2 of the common ways it can be done so is by either goofing around with ACPI events (uncomfortable for most ppl and not easily reproducible for me atleast) or via systemd services (easily reproducible and implement)

The implementation in question is https://geoff.greer.fm/2018/01/02/linux-laptop-locking/ . Where the author goes over locking the screen when `suspend` state is detected. The systemd unit in question is 

```
[Unit]
 Description=Lock the screen
+Before=sleep.target
 
 [Service]
 User=ggreer
 Environment=DISPLAY=:0
 ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/lock-screen
 
 [Install]
-WantedBy=suspend.target
+WantedBy=sleep.target
```

Here, the `Environment` parameter is of interest, from what I can see, this is an X11 thing. What is the Wayland (or precisely, Hyprland) equivalent of this?

title: Add Option to move Workspace to current Monitor
body:
### Description

It would be nice to have the option of moving a workspace to the monitor where the cursor currently is. This would be useful for moving around Workspaces in multi-monitor setups. I currently do this using `hyprctl` (as seen below) but my approach is kinda hacky (as seen below :D) and I think having this as a default functionality in Hyprland would be nice.

For anybody stumbling over this Issue, here's a bit of config I wrote to add this functionality using hyprctl and grep:
> Note that I'm getting the current monitor from the active Window, so when there is no active window on the current monitor, this might not work correctly
```
bind = $mainMod CONTROL, 1, exec, hyprctl dispatch moveworkspacetomonitor 1 $(hyprctl activewindow | egrep "monitor: [[:digit:]]+" | egrep -o "[[:digit:]]+") && hyprctl dispatch workspace 1

body:
### Hyprland Version

Hyprland, built from branch  at commit b08b72358ad549fd066e5be0fc3aa4c9df367607 dirty (). Tag: v0.27.2  flags: (if any)

### Bug or Regression?

Bug

### Description

In both places where Hyprland calls xkb_keymap_new_from_file, it calls fopen() on the keymap file, and then doesn't close it. xkb_keymap_new_from_file doesn't it automatically.  Any processes started by Hyprland inherit these open file descriptors.

Set kb_file in the input section of the config to a keymap file, and reload configuration a few times, to leak the file multiple times. Then check how many open files Hyprland has in `/proc/$HYPRLANDS_PID/fd`.

title: Nix: corrections for overlays, overrideable systems
body:
Nearly identical to <https://github.com/hyprwm/xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland/pull/75> and <https://github.com/hyprwm/hyprland-protocols/pull/6>. Copied message and edited below.

1. The `nix fmt` command did not work for me so I have reverted it to use `legacyPackages` for simplicity. It works now.
   - Ran `nix fmt` on the whole flake, however the `overlays` in the `import nixpkgs` in `flake.nix` has some comments that get messed up when Alejandra has its way. I dislike Alejandra.
2. The overlay `hyprland-packages` used to include some dependencies (`udis86`) but not all of them. That was the job of the `default` overlay. I have changed it so that `hyprland-packages` will work correctly on its own, as now it includes all dependency overlays.
   - Now each package has its own overlay, while `default` combines the ones an end-user is expected to need.
   - ```nix
     $ nix eval 'path:.#overlays' --apply 'builtins.attrNames'
     [ "default" "hyprland-extras" "hyprland-packages" "udis86" "waybar-hyprland" "wlroots-hyprland" ]
     ```
3. Versions now use string interpolation rather than concatenation, because it looks nicer than when Alejandra tries to wrap concatenated strings.
   - ~~Perhaps we should adopt my (unpublished) changes from `Alexays/Waybar` and pull the first version fragment from `meson.build`.~~ The `props.json` file takes care of that. Maybe the other flakes could learn a thing or two?
4. Added another input `nix-systems` so that the `systems` is overrideable. I like this much better than using `flake-utils` or `flake-parts`.
   - Using `default-linux`, which is `[ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" ]`.
   - Updated usage when importing `nixpkgs` to correct for undocumented deprecation of `system`.
   - https://github.com/nix-systems/nix-systems
   - **Blocker:** This PR depends on <https://github.com/hyprwm/hyprland-protocols/pull/6> and for now you will see an error when evaluating flake outputs.
5. The attributes of the `packages` output are inherited from internal `pkgsFor`, which contains all of the overlays pre-applied.
   - ```nix
     $ nix eval 'path:.#packages.x86_64-linux' --apply 'builtins.attrNames'
     [ "default" "hyprland" "hyprland-debug" "hyprland-hidpi" "hyprland-no-hidpi" "hyprland-nvidia" "hyprland-protocols" "hyprland-share-picker" "hyprland-unwrapped" "udis86" "waybar-hyprland" "wlroots-hyprland" "xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland" ]
     ```

title: Do not enable VRR on HDMI and DVI connected displays.
body:
### Hyprland Version

0.27.2-1

### Bug or Regression?

Bug

### Description

Current in-kernel graphics drivers on Linux supports VRR via VESA's Adaptive Sync, which is only on DisplayPort. HDMI and DVI (and I guess VGA too, but c'mon) will not work properly if `misc { vrr=1 }` is added to the config. If HDMI/DVI does get VRR support in the future, revert this.

Or give us the option to enable VRR per monitor, like we can on sway.

### How to reproduce

Plug in a monitor via DisplayPort (or don't if you're on a laptop, since it's likely using embedded DisplayPort) and one via HDMI or DVI, then enable VRR in the config.

Your non-DP monitor will start to act up and go blank and piss and cry all over the place.

_No response_
